definition_zh: 回归；倒退；（统计学）回归分析、回归模型；（疾病）消退；（海平面下降造成的）海退
definition_en: a return to an earlier or worse state, or the statistical method that estimates how variables are related to an outcome
core_image: 散点图上一条线穿过云一样的点，最偏的点被慢慢拉回中间
scene: 实验室里，学生把两年的成绩画成散点图，想看出每天多学一小时能带来多少分。The team used a regression to see how study hours predicted exam scores.
sceneCN: 这里 regression 指「用数据估计变量之间关系的统计方法」（第 2 个义项：回归分析）；句意：研究小组用一次回归分析看学习时长如何预测考试分数。图中可辨识物件：散点图、拟合直线、坐标轴、记录表。

pos.zh: 回归；倒退；回归分析；消退

senses.title: A step back to a former state
senses.definition: a movement back to an earlier condition, especially one that is worse or less advanced
senses.definitionCN: 退回从前的状况，尤指退到更差或更落后的状态
senses.example: The village saw a regression into old habits after the factory closed.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后，这个村子又退回了旧习惯。
senses.why: Regressio is literally a stepping back, so the word names any movement that reverses an advance.
senses.whyCN: regressio 本义是往回走一步，因此可指任何让进展倒退的变化。

senses.title: The statistical method of fitting a relation
senses.titleCN: 拟合变量关系的统计方法
senses.definition: the statistical technique that estimates how one or more input variables are related to an outcome
senses.definitionCN: 估计一个或多个输入变量与结果之间关系的统计方法
senses.example: The team ran a regression to test whether study hours predicted scores.
senses.exampleCN: 研究小组做了一次回归分析，检验学习时长能否预测分数。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century work on inherited traits gave this name to a method that measures how one variable moves with another.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪研究遗传特征的工作，把测量一个变量随另一个变量变化的方法定名为回归。

senses.title: The fitted line itself
senses.definition: the line or curve drawn through a cloud of data points to summarise the estimated relationship
senses.definitionCN: 穿过一堆数据点、用来概括估计关系的直线或曲线
senses.example: Each extra hour raised the regression line by four points.
senses.exampleCN: 每多学一小时，回归线上移四分。
senses.why: Once a relation is estimated it is drawn, and the drawing borrows the name of the method that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 关系一旦被估计出来就要画成线，这条线便沿用了产生它的方法之名。

senses.title: Extremes drifting back toward the average
senses.definition: the tendency of unusually high or low measurements to move closer to the average when measured again
senses.definitionCN: 异常偏高或偏低的测量值在再次测量时向平均值靠拢的倾向
senses.example: The second test showed regression to the mean among the top scorers.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次测验中，高分者出现了向平均值回归的现象。
senses.why: An extreme score contains more luck than usual, so a repeat measurement tends to drift back toward the centre.
senses.whyCN: 极端分数里包含比平常更多的运气成分，再测一次就容易向中间漂。

senses.title: A family of extended models
senses.definition: one of the model variants that add several predictors or handle a categorical outcome
senses.definitionCN: 增加多个预测变量、或处理分类结果的一类模型变体
senses.example: Logistic regression suits a yes-or-no outcome better than a straight line.
senses.exampleCN: 结果只有是或否时，逻辑回归比一条直线更合适。
senses.why: The same fitting idea branches into variants when the inputs multiply or the outcome becomes a category.
senses.whyCN: 当输入变量增多或结果变成类别，同一套拟合思路就分出多种变体。

senses.title: A disease or tumour retreating
senses.definition: the shrinking or retreat of a disease, growth or tumour under treatment
senses.definitionCN: 疾病、增生物或肿瘤在治疗下缩小、退去
senses.example: The scan showed regression of the tumour after six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 六周后的扫描显示肿瘤已经消退。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word for a disease that steps back from the body it had invaded.
senses.whyCN: 医学借这个词表示疾病从它侵占的身体部位退回去。

senses.title: A child losing learned skills
senses.titleCN: 儿童失去已学会的技能
senses.definition: the loss of skills a child had already acquired, such as speech, play or toilet use
senses.definitionCN: 儿童失去已经掌握的技能，如说话、玩耍或如厕
senses.example: The parents reported a regression in their son's speech.
senses.exampleCN: 父母说儿子的语言能力出现了倒退。
senses.why: A child who loses ground is stepping backward along the developmental path, which is the oldest image of the word.
senses.whyCN: 孩子失去已有的进展，就是沿发育路径往回走，正是这个词最古老的意象。

senses.title: The sea withdrawing from the land
senses.definition: the retreat of the shoreline, usually caused by falling sea level or rising land
senses.definitionCN: 海岸线后退，通常由海平面下降或陆地抬升引起
senses.example: The sandstone records a regression of the sea in the Jurassic.
senses.exampleCN: 这片砂岩记录了侏罗纪的一次海退。
senses.why: Geology treats the shoreline as a line that can step back, reusing the same image as the general sense.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把海岸线看成一条可以后退的线，沿用了一般义项里的同一意象。

intro.en: Regression comes from Latin regressio 'a going back', a noun of action from regredi 'to step back', built on re- 'back' plus gradi 'to step'. English took the word through French in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: regression 出自拉丁 regressio「退回」，是 regredi「往回走」的名词形式，由 re-「向后」加 gradi「走」构成。英语十六世纪经法语引入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gradus meant 'step, pace', and it also gives English grade, gradual and graduate; the step is the physical core of the family.
items.cn: gradus 意为「步、步伐」，也衍生出英语 grade、gradual 与 graduate；「步」是这一族词的实体核心。

items.en: Gradi was a deponent verb 'to step, go', built on the same stem; progress, regress and retrograde all combine a direction prefix with this verb.
items.cn: gradi 是异态动词「迈步、走」，词干相同；progress、regress 与 retrograde 都是方向前缀加这个动词。

items.en: Re- 'back' plus gradi produced regredi 'to step back, return', which describes a physical withdrawal before it describes a statistical one.
items.cn: re-「向后」加 gradi 构成 regredi「往回走、返回」，先描述身体后退，后才用于统计。

items.en: Regressio was the noun of action, 'a going back'; it entered English through French as a general word for a return or a backward movement.
items.cn: regressio 是动作名词「退回」，经法语进入英语，最初泛指返回或后退。

items.en: Francis Galton used the term in the 1880s for the tendency of extreme inherited traits to move toward the average, and regression later became the name of the fitting method itself.
items.cn: 高尔顿在一八八〇年代用这个词描述极端遗传特征向平均值靠拢的倾向，后来 regression 又成为整套拟合方法的名称。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin regressio, attested in the classical language, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact date of its first English use is not recorded. The pre-Latin origin of gradus is reconstructed rather than attested, and the reconstruction is offered as a form, not as a demonstrated word.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 regressio，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的确切年代没有记录。gradus 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构形式而非有据可查，该形式只是重构，并非已证实的词。

note.en: Group one follows the gradi stock, where a direction prefix decides whether a step goes forward, backward or sideways; group two holds ordinary words for going back to a previous state.
note.cn: 第一组同出 gradi 词干，方向前缀决定这一步是向前、向后还是绕行；第二组是表达回到从前状态的普通词。

entries.definition: To go back to an earlier or worse state; the verb without the statistical noun ending.
entries.definitionCN: 回到更早或更差的状态；是不带统计名词后缀的动词形式。

entries.definition: Pro- 'forward' plus gradi: a step in the other direction, so the two words are mirror images.
entries.definitionCN: pro-「向前」加 gradi：朝相反方向迈步，两词正好互为镜像。

entries.definition: Retro- 'backward' plus gradi: moving backward, used of planets, steps or policies.
entries.definitionCN: retro-「向后」加 gradi：向后移动，用于行星、步骤或政策。

entries.definition: From gradus 'step': happening one step at a time, with no statistical sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 gradus「步」：一步一步发生，完全不含统计义。

entries.definition: The plain word for coming back to a place or state, carrying no judgement about whether it is worse.
entries.definitionCN: 回到某地或某状态的普通说法，不判断变好还是变坏。

entries.definition: A return of illness after improvement, close to the medical sense of regression but used of patients rather than scans.
entries.definitionCN: 病情好转后又复发，接近 regression 的医学义，但多用于病人而非影像。

entries.definition: A going back to an earlier form or type, often in biology, without the fitted-line sense.
entries.definitionCN: 回到早先形态或类型，常用于生物学，不含拟合线之义。

entries.definition: A fall in quality or amount; it stresses loss rather than the act of stepping back.
entries.definitionCN: 质量或数量下降；强调损失，而非往回走这个动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin step, the statistical line and the real medical and geological uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的「步」、统计里的那条线，以及真实的医学与地质用法。

normal.en: Re- 'back' plus gradi 'to step': one step backward.
normal.cn: re-「向后」加 gradi「走」：往回迈一步。

normal.en: The same family gives progress, retrograde and gradual.
normal.cn: 同族词给出 progress、retrograde 与 gradual。

normal.en: In statistics the line makes extreme points drift back to the middle.
normal.cn: 统计里那条线让偏远的点漂回中间。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: linear regression, regression analysis, regression to the mean.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：线性回归、回归分析、向平均值回归。

normal.en: Medicine says a tumour regresses when it shrinks.
normal.cn: 医学说肿瘤消退时也用这个词。

abstract.en: Picture a hiker who turns around one step before the summit.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者在离山顶一步时转身往回走。

abstract.en: Picture a graph line quietly pulling the furthest dots inward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条图线把最远的点悄悄拉回内侧。

abstract.en: Picture a shoreline moving away from the houses it once reached.
abstract.cn: 想象海岸线从它曾抵达的房屋前退开。

examples.en: A single regression cannot prove causation, only a measured association.
examples.cn: 一次回归分析不能证明因果，只能给出测得的关联。

examples.en: The report described a regression in reading skills among younger pupils.
examples.cn: 报告描述了低年级学生阅读能力的倒退。

examples.en: Geologists read the rock layer as evidence of a marine regression.
examples.cn: 地质学家把这一岩层读作海退的证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）+ gress（走）」——往回走：回归、倒退；统计里让点回到线附近

root: 拉丁 regressio「退回」= regredi（re-「向后」+ gradi「走」）的名词形式；gradi 出自 gradus「步」。同根词有 progress、retrograde、gradual。英语经法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one backward step: a return to a worse state, a measured relation, the line that draws it, extremes drifting inward, a family of models, a tumour retreating, a child losing skills and a shoreline withdrawing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次「往回走」：退回更差的状态、被测量的关系、画出关系的线、极端值向内漂、扩展出的模型家族、肿瘤消退、孩子失去技能，以及海岸线后退。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one step taken backward, away from where the path had reached.
core.cn: 核心意象：朝后迈出一步，离开原本已经走到的地方。

branches.en: GOING BACK: a village losing its habits and a tumour shrinking are the same backward step at different scales.
branches.cn: 往回走：村子丢掉新习惯与肿瘤缩小，是同一后退动作在不同尺度上的样子。

branches.en: MEASURE THEN DRAW: the method estimates a relation and the line makes that estimate visible.
branches.cn: 先测量再画线：方法估计出关系，线把估计结果画出来。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE PULLS: extreme scores contain luck, so a repeat drifts toward the average.
branches.cn: 中间有拉力：极端分数含运气，重测就向平均值漂。

branches.en: THE FAMILY GROWS: more predictors and categorical outcomes split one fitting idea into variants.
branches.cn: 家族扩张：更多预测变量与分类结果，把一套拟合思路分成多种变体。

branches.en: SMALL AND LARGE RETREATS: a child losing speech and a sea leaving the land both move backward from a reached line.
branches.cn: 小尺度与大尺度的退却：孩子失去语言与海水离开陆地，都是从已抵达的界线后退。

intro.en: Regression is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a noun ending, and every piece also builds other English words.
intro.cn: regression 由拉丁前缀、拉丁动词词根与名词词尾构成，每一部分也都参与构成别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Re- 'back' combines with gradi 'to step'; gradus 'step' supplies grade, gradual and graduate, while -io forms action nouns such as regressio.
latinIntro.cn: re-「向后」与 gradi「走」组合；gradus「步」衍生 grade、gradual 与 graduate，-io 则构成 regressio 这类动作名词。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of the step.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把步伐的方向反过来。

items.example: Grade and gradual both descend from this noun.
items.exampleCN: grade 与 gradual 都出自这个名词。

items.example: Every direction prefix needs this verb to make a motion word.
items.exampleCN: 每个方向前缀都要配这个动词才能造出运动词。

items.example: The verb describes the body before it describes data.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词先描述身体，再用于数据。

items.example: The Latin noun became the English word through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词经法语变成英语词。

items.example: Skills can regress without practice.
items.exampleCN: 技能不练就会倒退。

items.example: The policy was criticised as regressive.
items.exampleCN: 这项政策被批评为倒退。

items.example: Progress is the mirror image of regress.
items.exampleCN: progress 正是 regress 的镜像。

items.example: The planet appears retrograde from Earth.
items.exampleCN: 从地球看这颗行星像在逆行。

items.example: The change was gradual rather than sudden.
items.exampleCN: 变化是逐步的，不是突然的。

latinEntries.structure: regredi, regressus sum (verb, deponent, third conjugation)

definition_zh: 线的；直线的；线性的；按顺序展开的；成正比例的；一维的
definition_en: consisting of or arranged along a line, or changing by a constant amount in direct proportion
core_image: 一根拉直的细线，从一端到另一端没有一处弯折
scene: 白板上只画了一条从角落拉到另一角的直线，没有分支也没有弯。The plotted curve falls in a strictly linear pattern as the years pass.
sceneCN: 这里 linear 指「沿直线、按固定比例变化的」（第 1 个义项：形状或变化保持直线关系）；句意：随着年份推移，这张图呈严格的线性下降。图中可辨识物件：白板、直尺、坐标轴、折线。

pos.zh: 直线的；线性的；成比例的

derivatives.zh: 直线构成的；沿直线运动的

senses.title: Shaped like or arranged along a line
senses.definition: forming a straight line or arranged in a line, with no bend or branch
senses.definitionCN: 构成一条直线或排成一行，没有弯折或分支
senses.example: The chairs stood in a linear row along the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 椅子沿墙排成一条直线。
senses.why: Linearis comes from linea 'a line', so the first sense simply repeats the shape of a drawn line.
senses.whyCN: linearis 出自 linea「线」，第一义就是把一条画出的线的形状说出来。

senses.title: Arranged in a fixed order
senses.definition: proceeding step by step in one fixed order, said of stories, arguments or processes
senses.definitionCN: 按一个固定次序一步步推进，用于故事、论证或流程
senses.example: The film tells a linear story from childhood to old age.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片按线性顺序讲一个从童年到老年的故事。
senses.why: A line has a direction, so a sequence that never jumps back and forth is pictured as a line.
senses.whyCN: 线有方向，因此从不来回跳跃的顺序就被想象成一条线。

senses.title: Changing by a constant rate
senses.definition: increasing or decreasing by a fixed amount for each unit of change in the other quantity
senses.definitionCN: 另一个量每变化一个单位，就按固定数量增加或减少
senses.example: Their savings showed linear growth of fifty pounds a month.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的存款每月固定增加五十英镑，呈线性增长。
senses.why: On a graph a constant rate draws a straight line, so the arithmetic of equal steps is called linear.
senses.whyCN: 在图上固定速率画出来就是直线，因此等步长的算术关系被称为线性。

senses.title: First-degree in algebra
senses.definition: containing variables only to the first power, with no squares, products or higher terms
senses.definitionCN: 变量只出现一次方，没有平方、乘积或更高次项
senses.example: Solve the linear equation before trying the quadratic one.
senses.exampleCN: 先解这个一次方程，再去碰二次方程。
senses.why: A first-degree equation plots as a straight line, which is why algebra borrowed the geometric name.
senses.whyCN: 一次方程画出来是直线，代数因此借用了几何的名字。

senses.title: Plain and uncomplicated reasoning
senses.definition: simple and direct, moving from one point to the next without side branches
senses.definitionCN: 简单直接，从一点推到下一点，不绕旁支
senses.example: A linear approach works here, with no need for negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 这里用简单直接的思路就行，不必反复磋商。
senses.why: Thinking that never loops back is pictured as walking a straight path, the same image as the geometry.
senses.whyCN: 不绕回来的思考被想象成走一条直路，与几何义是同一幅画。

senses.title: Measured in one dimension
senses.definition: measured along a single dimension, such as length, rather than area or volume
senses.definitionCN: 沿单一维度测量，如长度，而非面积或体积
senses.example: The survey recorded linear measure in metres, not area.
senses.exampleCN: 这次测量记录的是以米计的长度，而不是面积。
senses.why: A line has length but no width, so a one-dimensional quantity is naturally called linear.
senses.whyCN: 线有长度没有宽度，一维的量自然被称为线性。

senses.title: Direct descent in a family
senses.definition: descending in an unbroken direct line from an ancestor, without collateral branches
senses.definitionCN: 从祖先一脉直传，不分出旁支
senses.example: The estate passed down the linear descent of the eldest son.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产业沿长子的直系血脉传下去。
senses.why: A family tree drawn as a single unbroken line gives the word its genealogical sense.
senses.whyCN: 把家谱画成一条不断的线，就得到这个词的谱系义。

senses.title: Proportional output in electronics
senses.definition: producing an output that rises or falls in direct proportion to the input, with no distortion
senses.definitionCN: 输出随输入按正比升降，不发生失真
senses.example: A linear amplifier keeps the wave shape unchanged.
senses.exampleCN: 线性放大器让波形保持不变。
senses.why: An undistorted signal keeps a one-to-one relation with its input, the electronic form of a straight line.
senses.whyCN: 不失真的信号与输入保持一一对应，就是直线关系在电子学里的形态。

intro.en: Linear is Latin linearis 'of a line', built on linea 'line, thread', which itself comes from linum 'flax'. English adopted the adjective in the seventeenth century, and mathematics later extended it to equations and proportional relations. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: linear 出自拉丁 linearis「线的」，由 linea「线、线绳」构成，而 linea 又出自 linum「亚麻」。英语十七世纪引入这个形容词，数学后来把它扩展到方程与比例关系。年代均为约数。

items.en: Linum meant 'flax', the plant whose fibres made the thread; linen also comes from this word.
items.cn: linum 意为「亚麻」，其纤维可以搓成线；linen 也出自这个词。

items.en: Linea was first a linen thread and then any drawn line; the physical thread is the origin of the geometric line.
items.cn: linea 最初指亚麻线，后来指任何画出的线；实体的线绳是几何直线的来源。

items.en: Linearis meant 'belonging to a line'; it described things laid out along a line before it described equations.
items.cn: linearis 意为「属于线的」，先形容沿直线排布的事物，后才用于方程。

items.en: English took the adjective from Latin, first for shapes and rows, and later for anything arranged in sequence.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语借入这个形容词，先用于形状与排列，后用于按顺序展开的事物。

items.en: The coordinate method of the seventeenth century showed that first-degree equations plot as straight lines, fixing the mathematical sense of linear.
items.cn: 十七世纪的坐标法证明一次方程画出来是直线，从而固定了 linear 的数学含义。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin linearis, attested in the classical language, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact date of its first English use is not recorded. The deeper origin of linum is not established, and no reconstructed root is asserted here.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 linearis，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的年代没有记录。linum 的更早来源没有定论，此处不给出重构词根。

note.en: Group one shares the linea stock, where Latin thread and line produce English words for straightness, ancestry and alignment; group two holds words that name the same simple geometry from another angle.
note.cn: 第一组共享 linea 词干，拉丁语的线与线绳衍生出表示笔直、血统与对齐的英语词；第二组从别的角度命名同一种简单几何。

entries.definition: The plain noun for a long thin mark; linear is the adjective built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 表示细长痕迹的普通名词；linear 是它派生出的形容词。

entries.definition: Descending in a direct line from an ancestor; it keeps the family-tree sense but not the equation sense.
entries.definitionCN: 从祖先直系传下；保留家谱义，却不含方程义。

entries.definition: A feature or outline of a face or landscape, from the same Latin line; it never means proportional.
entries.definitionCN: 面部或地貌的轮廓线条，同出拉丁 linea；从不表示成比例。

entries.definition: From French aligner, ultimately linea: to bring things onto a shared line, the verb behind alignment.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语 aligner 上溯到 linea：把东西排到同一条线上，也是 alignment 的动词。

entries.definition: Having no bend; it describes the shape but not proportional change or first-degree equations.
entries.definitionCN: 没有弯折；只描述形状，不表示比例变化或一次方程。

entries.definition: Following in order, one after another; it covers the narrative sense without the geometric one.
entries.definitionCN: 按次序一个接一个；覆盖叙事义，但不含几何义。

entries.definition: Changing by a fixed ratio; close to the growth sense but says nothing about a drawn line.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定比率变化；接近增长义，但不涉及画出的线。

entries.definition: Having a single dimension; it matches the length sense and is never used for algebra.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一个维度；对应长度义，从不用于代数。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin thread behind the word, the straight graph and the real phrases that carry it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：词后那条亚麻线的来历、图上的直线，以及真正固定它的搭配。

normal.en: Linea 'thread' plus -aris: a thread stretched tight.
normal.cn: linea「线绳」加 -aris：一根拉紧的线。

normal.en: A constant rate draws a straight line on a graph.
normal.cn: 固定速率在图上画出来就是直线。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: linear equation, linear growth, linear model.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：线性方程、线性增长、线性模型。

normal.en: The opposite is nonlinear, built with the negative prefix non-.
normal.cn: 反义是 nonlinear，由否定前缀 non- 构成。

normal.en: Lineal keeps the family-tree sense that linear also carries.
normal.cn: lineal 保存了 linear 同样具备的家谱义。

abstract.en: Picture a single thread pulled from one corner of a board to the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线从板子的一角拉到另一角。

abstract.en: Picture equal steps on a staircase, never wider and never narrower.
abstract.cn: 想象楼梯上等宽的每一级，不忽宽忽窄。

abstract.en: Picture a story told from birth to old age with no flashback.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从出生讲到老年、没有倒叙的故事。

examples.en: The data fit a linear model far better than a curved one.
examples.cn: 数据与线性模型的吻合程度远好于曲线模型。

examples.en: She preferred a linear plot because the audience could follow it easily.
examples.cn: 她偏爱线性情节，因为观众容易跟上。

examples.en: The engineer checked that the amplifier stayed linear across the whole range.
examples.cn: 工程师检查了放大器在整个范围内是否保持线性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「line（线）+ ar」——像线一样直：直线的、线性的、成比例的

root: 拉丁 linearis「线的」= linea（线、亚麻线，出自 linum「亚麻」）+ -alis（属于……的）。英语十七世纪借入。同根词有 line、lineal、lineament、align。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep to one line: a drawn straight shape, a fixed sequence, a constant rate, a first-degree equation, plain reasoning, one-dimensional measure, direct descent and an undistorted electronic output.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都守着同一条线：画出的直线形状、固定顺序、固定速率、一次方程、简单思路、一维长度、直系血统，以及不失真的电子输出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread stretched straight, with no bend, fork or loop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被拉直的线，不弯、不分叉、不打圈。

branches.en: SHAPE AND MEASURE: a line has length but no breadth, so the drawn form and the one-dimensional quantity are the same object.
branches.cn: 形状与度量：线有长度没有宽度，画出的形状与一维的量正是同一个对象。

branches.en: UNBROKEN ORDER: a story with no flashback and a family with no side branch are both single continuous lines.
branches.cn: 不断的顺序：没有倒叙的故事与没有旁支的家族，都是唯一一条连续的线。

branches.en: RATE AND EQUATION: equal steps give a constant slope, and a first-degree equation plots as that slope.
branches.cn: 速率与方程：等步长给出固定斜率，一次方程画出来就是这条斜线。

branches.en: PLAIN THINKING: reasoning that never loops back walks the same straight path with the feet of the mind.
branches.cn: 简单思路：不绕回来的推理，是用心思的脚步走同一条直路。

branches.en: FAITHFUL OUTPUT: an undistorted signal keeps a one-to-one relation with its input, a straight line in electronics.
branches.cn: 忠实输出：不失真的信号与输入保持一一对应，就是电子学里的直线。

intro.en: Linear is a Latin adjective built on a noun and a suffix, and the same pieces also build the geometry, the family words and the everyday verb for alignment.
intro.cn: linear 是由名词加后缀构成的拉丁形容词，同样的构件也造出几何词、家族词与表示对齐的日常动词。

latinIntro.en: Linea 'thread' yields line, lineal, lineament and align; -alis 'belonging to' survives as -al in English, and non- negates the whole adjective.
latinIntro.cn: linea「线绳」衍生 line、lineal、lineament 与 align；-alis「属于……」在英语留下 -al，non- 则否定整个形容词。

items.example: The plant gave both the thread and the word for linen.
items.exampleCN: 这种植物既提供线绳，也提供了亚麻布的名称。

items.example: The thread became the geometric line.
items.exampleCN: 线绳变成了几何上的线。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: The growth was linear for five years.
items.exampleCN: 五年里增长是线性的。

items.example: The test measured the linearity of the sensor.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试测量传感器的线性度。

items.meaning: in a straight or proportional way
items.example: The values rise linearly with temperature.
items.exampleCN: 数值随温度线性上升。

items.example: The title passed by lineal succession.
items.exampleCN: 爵位按直系继承传下。

items.example: The lineaments of the coast were clear from above.
items.exampleCN: 从高处看海岸的轮廓很清楚。

items.example: Align the two edges before gluing.
items.exampleCN: 粘合前先把两条边对齐。

items.example: The spring behaves nonlinear once stretched far.
items.exampleCN: 这根弹簧拉得很长后表现为非线性。

definition_zh: 非线性的；非直线的；不成比例的；（叙事、剪辑）不按固定顺序的
definition_en: not forming a straight line and not changing in direct proportion, or not following one fixed sequence
core_image: 一条越走越陡的曲线，起点平缓，末端几乎竖起来
scene: 同一组数据被画成曲线，输入翻倍时输出涨了三倍。The response became nonlinear once the amplifier reached its limit.
sceneCN: 这里 nonlinear 指「输出与输入不再成比例」（第 2 个义项：不成正比的响应）；句意：放大器到达极限后，响应就变成非线性的了。图中可辨识物件：曲线图、放大器、输入旋钮、输出表。

derivatives.zh: 非线性的（带连字符写法）
使非线性化（技术文献，罕用）

senses.title: Not a straight line on a graph
senses.definition: appearing as a curve rather than a straight line when plotted
senses.definitionCN: 画在图上呈曲线，而不是直线
senses.example: The fitted curve is nonlinear and bends sharply at the end.
senses.exampleCN: 拟合出的曲线是非线性的，末端急剧弯曲。
senses.why: Non- negates linear, and linear first meant line-shaped, so the word begins as a denial of straightness.
senses.whyCN: non- 否定 linear，而 linear 首先表示线形，所以这个词一开始就是对「直」的否认。

senses.title: Out of proportion to the input
senses.definition: responding by a different ratio, so that doubling the input more than doubles or less than doubles the output
senses.definitionCN: 响应的比率不同，输入加倍时输出可能超过两倍，也可能不到两倍
senses.example: The spring becomes nonlinear under heavy loads.
senses.exampleCN: 这根弹簧在重载下表现出非线性。
senses.why: Proportional change draws a straight line, so losing proportion and losing straightness are one event.
senses.whyCN: 按比例变化画出来是直线，因此失去比例与失去直线性其实是同一件事。

senses.title: Containing higher powers or products
senses.definition: containing squared, cubed or multiplied variables, so that no single straight-line solution exists
senses.definitionCN: 含平方、立方或变量乘积，因而没有单一直线解
senses.example: That nonlinear equation has two separate solutions.
senses.exampleCN: 那个非线性方程有两个不同的解。
senses.why: A squared term bends the curve, which is the algebraic reason the equation can no longer be a line.
senses.whyCN: 平方项让曲线弯折，这就是方程不再是直线的代数原因。

senses.title: Sensitive dynamics that do not settle
senses.titleCN: 对初值敏感、难以收敛的动态
senses.definition: describing systems whose behaviour is sensitive to small changes and cannot be predicted by simple proportional rules
senses.definitionCN: 描述对微小变化敏感、无法用简单比例规则预测的系统
senses.example: Weather is a classic nonlinear system with sensitive beginnings.
senses.exampleCN: 天气是典型的非线性系统，初始条件十分敏感。
senses.why: When outputs feed back into inputs, small differences grow, and the tidy line of proportionality disappears.
senses.whyCN: 当输出又回到输入形成反馈，微小差异会被放大，成比例的整齐直线就消失了。

senses.title: A story that jumps in time
senses.definition: telling events out of chronological order, with flashbacks, parallel threads or repeated scenes
senses.definitionCN: 不按时间顺序叙述，使用倒叙、并行线索或重复场景
senses.example: The novel uses a nonlinear structure that begins at the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说采用非线性结构，从葬礼写起。
senses.why: A sequence that does not advance in one straight line is pictured as a bent path, the same image as the graph.
senses.whyCN: 不沿一条直线推进的顺序被想象成弯折的路径，与图上的曲线是同一意象。

senses.title: Distorted output in electronics
senses.definition: producing an output that no longer matches the input waveform, so that the signal is clipped or bent
senses.definitionCN: 输出不再与输入波形一致，信号被削顶或弯折
senses.example: Push the microphone too hard and the recording turns nonlinear.
senses.exampleCN: 话筒推得太狠，录音就会变成非线性。
senses.why: Clipping destroys the one-to-one relation between input and output, which is exactly the loss of a straight line.
senses.whyCN: 削顶破坏了输入与输出的一一对应，正相当于失去那条直线。

senses.title: Editing with instant access
senses.definition: editing video or audio by jumping directly to any frame, rather than winding through tape in order
senses.definitionCN: 直接跳到任意画面进行剪辑，而不是沿磁带顺序卷动
senses.example: Nonlinear editing lets the editor cut the last scene first.
senses.exampleCN: 非线性剪辑让剪辑师可以先剪最后一场。
senses.why: Tape forces a single forward path; random access breaks that path, so the workflow is called nonlinear.
senses.whyCN: 磁带只允许一条向前的路径，随机访问打破这条路径，于是这种流程被称为非线性。

senses.title: Thinking in leaps rather than steps
senses.titleCN: 跳跃式而非逐步式思考
senses.definition: reasoning by sudden connections and side paths instead of a single orderly chain of steps
senses.definitionCN: 靠突然的联想与旁路推理，而不是一条整齐的步骤链
senses.example: Her nonlinear thinking found a link the linear plan had missed.
senses.exampleCN: 她的跳跃式思考找到了线性计划漏掉的关联。
senses.why: Thought that branches and loops is drawn as a curve or a network, not as the straight path of step-by-step logic.
senses.whyCN: 会分叉、会回环的思路被画成曲线或网络，而不是逐步逻辑的直路。

intro.en: Nonlinear is an English compound of non- 'not' and linear, which itself goes back to Latin linea 'line'. The word is not a Latin formation: Latin supplied the negative particle and the adjective separately. It spread with mathematics and engineering in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nonlinear 是英语复合词，由 non-「不」加 linear 构成，而 linear 可上溯到拉丁 linea「线」。这个词并非拉丁语造词：拉丁语分别提供了否定词与形容词。它随数学与工程在十九、二十世纪推广。年代均为约数。

items.en: Non was a Latin adverb and negative particle meaning 'not'; English uses it freely as a prefix, as in nonsense and nonstop.
items.cn: non 是拉丁副词与否定小品词，意为「不」；英语自由地把它当否定前缀用，如 nonsense 与 nonstop。

items.en: Linea 'line, thread' is the source of linear; the geometric meaning of straightness is the part that non- denies.
items.cn: linea「线、线绳」是 linear 的来源；non- 否定的正是其中「直」这一几何含义。

items.en: English joined non- and linear to name anything that departs from a straight line or a fixed ratio; the compound is English, not Latin.
items.cn: 英语把 non- 与 linear 拼在一起，指任何偏离直线或固定比例的事物；这个复合词属英语，不是拉丁语。

items.en: Nineteenth-century work on differential equations and mechanics gave nonlinear equations and nonlinear systems their technical footing.
items.cn: 十九世纪关于微分方程与力学的工作，为非线性方程与非线性系统奠定了技术基础。

items.en: Chaos theory, electronics and digital editing each took the word for a different departure from a predictable straight path.
items.cn: 混沌理论、电子学与数字剪辑各自用这个词表示一种对可预测直路的偏离。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the word is a transparent English compound of non- and linear, so its formation is not in doubt; only the earliest recorded English use is undated. The deeper origin of linea is not established, and no reconstructed root is asserted.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：这个词是 non- 与 linear 构成的透明英语复合词，构词方式并不存疑；只是英语最早用例没有确切年代。linea 的更早来源无定论，此处不给出重构词根。

note.en: Group one holds the linear stock, where non- reverses or names the absence of straightness; group two holds words for curves, growth and disorder that are often confused with nonlinear.
note.cn: 第一组是 linear 一族，non- 在其中表示否定或「缺乏直线性」；第二组是常与非线性混淆的曲线、增长与无序类词。

entries.definition: Straight and proportional; the exact property that nonlinear denies.
entries.definitionCN: 笔直且成比例；正是 nonlinear 所否定的性质。

entries.definition: The quality of being nonlinear, often written with a hyphen in British texts.
entries.definitionCN: 非线性的性质，英式文本中常带连字符。

entries.definition: The hyphenated form of the same adjective; hyphenation does not change the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的带连字符写法，连字符不改变词义。

entries.definition: Of direct descent; it looks related but belongs to family trees, not curves.
entries.definitionCN: 指直系血统；看起来相关，却属于家谱而非曲线。

entries.definition: Bent rather than straight; it describes the picture but says nothing about proportionality.
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲而非笔直；只描述图形，不涉及比例。

entries.definition: Growing by a constant ratio; a frequent nonlinear pattern, but not every nonlinear relation is exponential.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定比率增长；一种常见的非线性形态，但并非所有非线性关系都是指数式。

entries.definition: Extremely sensitive to initial conditions; it names a kind of dynamics, not a departure from a line.
entries.definitionCN: 对初始条件极敏感；命名一种动态行为，而不是偏离直线。

entries.definition: Not even or uniform; an everyday word that carries no mathematical definition.
entries.definitionCN: 不均匀、不规整；日常用词，没有数学定义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the English negative prefix, the Latin line it denies, and the real technical and artistic uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：英语否定前缀、它所否定的拉丁「线」，以及真实的技术与艺术用法。

normal.en: Non- 'not' plus linear: literally not a line.
normal.cn: non-「不」加 linear：字面就是「不是线」。

normal.en: Doubling the input more than doubles the output: that is the proportion breaking.
normal.cn: 输入加倍而输出超过两倍，就是比例断掉了。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: nonlinear equation, nonlinear dynamics, nonlinear editing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：非线性方程、非线性动力学、非线性剪辑。

normal.en: Hyperlinked and hyphenated spellings both occur: non-linear is only a variant.
normal.cn: 连字符写法 non-linear 只是变体，词义不变。

normal.en: The core mathematics goes back to nineteenth-century differential equations.
normal.cn: 核心数学用法可追到十九世纪的微分方程。

abstract.en: Picture a path that starts flat and then climbs almost vertically.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路先平缓，随后几乎竖直向上。

abstract.en: Picture a film that opens at a funeral and then jumps to a childhood.
abstract.cn: 想象一部电影从葬礼开场，再跳回童年。

abstract.en: Picture a small nudge at the start growing into a completely different outcome.
abstract.cn: 想象开头一个轻推，最后长成完全不同的结果。

examples.en: The model had to account for nonlinear effects near the melting point.
examples.cn: 这个模型必须考虑熔点附近的非线性效应。

examples.en: Nonlinear editing replaced the old tape-based workflow.
examples.cn: 非线性剪辑取代了旧的磁带流程。

examples.en: A nonlinear narrative can feel confusing if the jumps are not motivated.
examples.cn: 如果跳跃缺少动机，非线性叙事会让人困惑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「non（不）+ linear（线）」——不是直线：非线性的、不成比例的

root: 英语复合词：non-（拉丁副词「不」）+ linear（拉丁 linearis，出自 linea「线」）。复合本身是英语构词，不是拉丁词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all deny one straight path: a bent curve, a broken proportion, higher powers, sensitive dynamics, a jumping story, a distorted signal, random-access editing and leaping thought.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在否认同一条直路：弯折的曲线、断掉的比例、更高次项、敏感的动态、跳跃的故事、失真的信号、随机访问的剪辑，以及跳跃的思路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that refuses to stay straight, bending further the more it is pushed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条不肯保持笔直的线，越推越弯。

branches.en: LEAVING THE STRAIGHT PATH: a curve, a broken ratio and a leap of thought all refuse to advance in equal steps.
branches.cn: 离开直路：曲线、断掉的比例与跳跃的思路，都拒绝按等步长前进。

branches.en: THE ALGEBRA OF BENDS: squared and multiplied terms are what make a line impossible.
branches.cn: 弯折的代数：平方项与乘积项使直线解不再存在。

branches.en: FEEDBACK GROWS: when output returns as input, tiny differences can expand beyond prediction.
branches.cn: 反馈放大：输出回到输入后，微小差异可能扩张到无法预测。

branches.en: JUMPING ORDER: flashbacks and random-access editing both break a single forward sequence.
branches.cn: 跳跃的顺序：倒叙与随机访问剪辑都打破了单一的向前顺序。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL BENDS: clipping destroys the one-to-one match between input and output.
branches.cn: 信号弯折：削顶破坏了输入与输出的一一对应。

intro.en: Nonlinear is an English compound: a Latin negative particle attached to an adjective that Latin built from a noun.
intro.cn: nonlinear 是英语复合词：拉丁否定小品词加一个由拉丁名词构成的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Non- 'not' is Latin in origin but freely used in English; linea and linearis supply the line, while non- has no noun family of its own.
latinIntro.cn: non-「不」源自拉丁，却在英语里自由使用；linea 与 linearis 提供「线」，而 non- 本身没有名词家族。

items.example: Non- simply denies the adjective that follows.
items.exampleCN: non- 只是否定后面那个形容词。

items.example: The Latin noun supplies the geometric core.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词提供几何核心。

items.example: Latin built the adjective; English later negated it.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语造出形容词，英语后来才加否定。

items.example: The positive adjective is the base of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 肯定形式的形容词是复合词的基底。

items.example: The response turned nonlinear at high load.
items.exampleCN: 高负载下响应变成非线性。

items.example: Engineers measure nonlinearity in decibels.
items.exampleCN: 工程师用分贝衡量非线性程度。

items.meaning: to make linear, often as an approximation
items.meaningCN: 使线性化，常作近似处理
items.example: They linearize the curve near the operating point.
items.exampleCN: 他们在工作点附近把曲线线性化。

items.example: The linearization holds only over a small range.
items.exampleCN: 这种线性化只在很小范围内成立。

definition_zh: 图；图表；曲线图；（数学）函数图像；（图论）由顶点与边构成的图；书写符号；用图表示
definition_en: a diagram showing how quantities are related, or a mathematical structure of points joined by links
core_image: 方格纸上一串数据点被折线连起来，旁边还画着几个互相连线的小圆点
scene: 黑板上左边是折线图，右边是几个小圆点和它们之间的连线。The tutor asked the class to read the graph before drawing any conclusion.
sceneCN: 这里 graph 指「显示数量关系的图表」（第 1 个义项：把数据画成可读的图形）；句意：老师让全班先读懂这张图，再下结论。图中可辨识物件：黑板、折线、坐标格、小圆点。

senses.title: A chart of data
senses.definition: a diagram in which numbers or quantities are shown as bars, points or lines so that a pattern becomes visible
senses.definitionCN: 用条形、点或线把数字或数量画出来、使规律可见的图
senses.example: The sales graph shows a steady rise since spring.
senses.exampleCN: 销售图表显示自春季以来稳步上升。
senses.why: Graph came into English as a short word for a drawn figure, and a drawn figure of numbers is the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: graph 进入英语时就是「画出来的图」的简称，把数字画出来便是最日常的义项。

senses.title: The plotted curve of a function
senses.definition: the set of points drawn on coordinate axes that shows the values taken by a mathematical function
senses.definitionCN: 在坐标轴上画出的点集，显示一个数学函数取到的值
senses.example: The graph of the function crosses the horizontal line twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这个函数的图像两次穿过水平线。
senses.why: Comparing a function to a picture of its values turns the abstract rule into a visible curve.
senses.whyCN: 把函数与它取值的样子对照，抽象规则就变成一条看得见的曲线。

senses.title: A network of points and links
senses.definition: a mathematical object made of points, called vertices, joined in pairs by links, called edges
senses.definitionCN: 由称为顶点的点、以及成对连接顶点的边所构成的数学对象
senses.example: Each city is a vertex in the transport graph.
senses.exampleCN: 在这张交通图里，每座城市都是一个顶点。
senses.why: A diagram of routes looks like dots joined by lines, so mathematics reused the everyday picture and made it precise.
senses.whyCN: 路线示意图看起来就是点加线，数学于是沿用这幅日常图景并把它精确化。

senses.title: A written symbol
senses.definition: a single letter or symbol used in writing, especially when treated as a unit of a writing system
senses.definitionCN: 书写中使用的单个字母或符号，尤指作为文字系统的一个单位
senses.example: The inscription has one unclear graph at the end.
senses.exampleCN: 这处铭文末尾有一个看不清的书写符号。
senses.why: Greek graphein meant 'to write or scratch', so the oldest layer of the word is a mark made by writing.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 graphein 意为「写、刻」，这个词最古老的一层就是写出来的记号。

senses.title: A map of social connections
senses.definition: a representation of people or accounts as points and their relationships as links, used by platforms and analysts
senses.definitionCN: 把人或账号表示为点、把关系表示为连线的表示法，供平台与分析者使用
senses.example: The social graph showed two clusters that barely touched.
senses.exampleCN: 社交关系图显示两个几乎没有交集的圈子。
senses.why: People and their friendships fit the dots-and-links picture exactly, so the technical network sense extends to society.
senses.whyCN: 人与朋友关系正好符合点加线的图景，技术上的网络义便延伸到社会关系。

senses.title: To plot data as a graph
senses.definition: to draw a chart or curve for a set of values, usually on axes
senses.definitionCN: 为一组数值画出图表或曲线，通常在坐标轴上
senses.example: The students graphed temperature against time.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们把温度随时间的变化画成图。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by the usual English route: put something into the form the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词按英语常见方式转动词：把东西做成名词所指的那种形式。

senses.title: To model a system as points and links
senses.titleCN: 把系统建模为点与连线
senses.definition: to represent a system as a set of vertices and edges so that its structure can be analysed
senses.definitionCN: 把一个系统表示成顶点与边的集合，以便分析其结构
senses.example: They graphed the citations to find the central papers.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把引用关系画成图，找出核心论文。
senses.why: The graph-theory noun supplies a verb for the act of building such a network model.
senses.whyCN: 图论名词提供了动词，用来表示建立这种网络模型的动作。

senses.title: A formal set of ordered pairs
senses.definition: the mathematical definition of a function's graph as the set of all ordered pairs of input and output
senses.definitionCN: 把函数图像严格定义为所有输入与输出有序对的集合
senses.example: By definition the graph is a set of ordered pairs.
senses.exampleCN: 按定义，图像就是一个有序对的集合。
senses.why: The picture on paper is only a shadow of the formal object, and mathematics names the object with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 纸上的图只是形式对象的影子，数学用同一个词来命名那个对象。

intro.en: Graph goes back to Greek graphē 'a writing, a drawing' and graphein 'to write, to scratch'. It reached English through French and Latin-derived forms in the nineteenth century, first as a short word for a drawn figure, then as a mathematical term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: graph 上溯到希腊 graphē「书写、图画」与 graphein「写、刻」。十九世纪经法语及拉丁语形式进入英语，先是「画出的图」的简称，后成为数学术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to write, draw or scratch', and the scratch of a stylus on a surface is the physical image behind the whole family.
items.cn: graphein 意为「写、画、刻」，笔尖在表面划出的痕迹是这一族词背后的实体意象。

items.en: Graphē was 'a writing or a drawing', the noun that Latin and later European languages borrowed for written and drawn things.
items.cn: graphē 意为「书写、图画」，拉丁语及后来的欧洲语言借它来表示写与画的事物。

items.en: Latin did not inherit the word; it borrowed graphium 'stylus' and graphicus 'of drawing' from Greek, which is why the family feels Greek rather than Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语并未继承这个词，而是从希腊语借入 graphium「刻笔」与 graphicus「绘画的」，所以这一族词更像希腊语而非拉丁语。

items.en: English graph began as a short term for a drawn figure, especially a chemical or mathematical diagram, before it named a data chart.
items.cn: 英语 graph 起初是「画出的图形」的简称，尤指化学或数学示意图，后来才指数据图表。

items.en: Twentieth-century graph theory fixed the dots-and-links sense, giving the word a formal definition as vertices and edges.
items.cn: 二十世纪的图论固定了点与连线的含义，把这个词正式定义为顶点与边。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Greek graphē, attested in Greek and passed on through Latin and French, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact date of its first English use is not recorded. The deeper origin of graphein is not established, and no reconstructed root is asserted.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的希腊语 graphē，并经拉丁语与法语转手，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的确切年代没有记录。graphein 的更早来源无定论，此处不给出重构词根。

note.en: Group one shares the Greek writing root, where a single element builds words for marks, drawings and the tools that make them; group two holds the everyday names for diagrams and networks.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊「写」词根，同一个构件造出记号、图画与作画工具的词；第二组是图表与网络的日常名称。

entries.definition: A single written symbol treated as a unit; it narrows the writing sense and has no chart meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一个单位看待的单个书写符号；收窄了书写义，不含图表义。

entries.definition: Relating to drawing, images or clear description; it describes the style rather than the chart.
entries.definitionCN: 与绘画、图像或清晰描述有关；描述的是风格，而不是那张图。

entries.definition: The carbon mineral used in pencils, named from the same writing root because it leaves marks.
entries.definitionCN: 铅笔用的碳矿物，因能留下痕迹而同样出自「写」这个词根。

entries.definition: Para- 'beside' plus graphein: a passage marked beside the text, a unit of writing rather than of data.
entries.definitionCN: para-「在旁边」加 graphein：在正文旁作标记的一段，是书写单位而非数据单位。

entries.definition: A visual display of information, often with bars or sectors; broader and less mathematical than graph.
entries.definitionCN: 信息的可视化展示，常用条形或扇形；比 graph 更宽泛，数学味更淡。

entries.definition: The set of points or the line drawn on axes, or the act of drawing it; it stresses the drawing event.
entries.definitionCN: 坐标轴上画出的一组点或线，也指绘制动作；强调画这个动作。

entries.definition: A simplified drawing that explains how parts relate; it need not involve numerical data.
entries.definitionCN: 解释各部分如何关联的简化画法，不一定涉及数值数据。

entries.definition: A set of connected things or people; it matches the graph-theory sense but is not a mathematical term.
entries.definitionCN: 一组相连的事物或人；对应图论义，但不是数学术语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek act of scratching a mark, the data chart and the dots-and-links structure.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊语「刻出记号」的动作、数据图表，以及点与连线的结构。

normal.en: Greek graphein 'to scratch a mark' is the root of the whole family.
normal.cn: 希腊 graphein「刻出记号」是这一族词的根。

normal.en: A graph of numbers is a picture of a relationship.
normal.cn: 数字的 graph 就是一段关系的画像。

normal.en: In graph theory the picture becomes dots joined by edges.
normal.cn: 在图论里，这幅画变成由边连接的点。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: bar graph, line graph, graph theory.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：条形图、折线图、图论。

normal.en: -graph also builds photograph, telegraph and paragraph.
normal.cn: -graph 还构成 photograph、telegraph 与 paragraph。

abstract.en: Picture a stylus scratching a line into a wax tablet.
abstract.cn: 想象一支刻笔在蜡板上划出一道线。

abstract.en: Picture a city map reduced to dots and the roads between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市地图被压缩成点和点之间的路。

abstract.en: Picture a friendship drawn as two dots with a single thread.
abstract.cn: 想象一段友谊被画成两个点和一根线。

examples.en: The graph makes the seasonal pattern obvious at a glance.
examples.cn: 这张图让人一眼看出季节性的规律。

examples.en: A graph with no cycles is called a tree in graph theory.
examples.cn: 在图论中，没有环的图称为树。

examples.en: She graphed the responses and found a clear peak in the middle.
examples.cn: 她把回答画成图，发现中间有一个明显的峰值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「graph（画、写）」——画出来的东西：图表；点与线连起来的图

root: 希腊 graphē「书写、图画」与 graphein「写、刻」；经法语及拉丁语转写形式进入英语。拉丁语本身没有继承这个词，只借入 graphium（刻笔）与 graphicus（绘画的）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a drawn chart to the curve of a function, the dots-and-links structure of graph theory, a written symbol, a social network, the two verbs of plotting and modelling, and finally the formal set of ordered pairs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从画出的图表走到函数曲线、图论的点线结构、书写符号、社交网络，再到绘图与建模两个动词，最后是形式化的有序对集合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: marks made on a surface so that a relation can be seen rather than merely stated.
core.cn: 核心意象：在表面上留下记号，让一段关系被看见，而不只是被说出来。

branches.en: CHARTING: the everyday diagram and the verb that produces it are one act seen as noun and action.
branches.cn: 作图：日常图表与产生它的动词，是同一个动作的名词面与动作面。

branches.en: THE CURVE AND ITS DEFINITION: the visible line on axes is the shadow of a formal set of ordered pairs.
branches.cn: 曲线与定义：坐标轴上看得见的线，是形式化有序对集合的影子。

branches.en: DOTS AND LINKS: the graph-theory object and the act of building it belong to the same structural view.
branches.cn: 点与连线：图论对象与建立它的动作，属于同一种结构视角。

branches.en: A MARK FOR WRITING: the oldest layer is a scratched symbol, the unit later called a grapheme.
branches.cn: 书写记号：最古老的一层是刻出的符号，后来被称为字素。

branches.en: PEOPLE AS POINTS: platforms reuse the dots-and-links picture for friendships and followers.
branches.cn: 人成为点：平台把点线图景挪用来表示友谊与关注。

intro.en: Graph is built from a Greek verb root that also became a suffix; the same element builds dozens of English words for writing, recording and drawing.
intro.cn: graph 由一个希腊动词词根构成，这个词根后来又变成后缀；同一构件造出大量表示书写、记录与绘制的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed graphium 'stylus' and graphicus 'of drawing' from Greek rather than inheriting them; English drew directly on the Greek noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语是从希腊语借入 graphium「刻笔」与 graphicus「绘画的」，而非继承；英语则直接取自希腊名词与动词。

items.example: The verb supplies the act behind every member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供这一族词背后的动作。

items.example: The noun became the English short word for a drawn figure.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词变成英语里「画出的图」的简称。

items.example: Telegraph and photograph both use this combining form.
items.exampleCN: telegraph 与 photograph 都用了这个构词成分。

items.structure: -graphy (combining form, 'the process of writing or recording')
items.example: Geography names the describing of the earth.
items.exampleCN: geography 指对大地的描述。

items.example: The graph of sales rose through the year.
items.exampleCN: 销售图表全年上升。

items.example: The report used graphic illustrations.
items.exampleCN: 报告使用了图形插图。

items.example: English has more graphemes than letters.
items.exampleCN: 英语的字素比字母多。

items.example: Graphite marks paper because of its layers.
items.exampleCN: 石墨因层状结构能在纸上留下痕迹。

items.example: Each paragraph makes one point.
items.exampleCN: 每一段讲一个要点。

items.example: Graphology claims to read character from writing.
items.exampleCN: 笔迹学声称能从字迹看出性格。

latinEntries.structure: graphium, graphii (n., second declension; borrowed from Greek grapheion)
graphicus, graphica, graphicum (adjective; from Greek graphikos)

definition_zh: 轴；坐标轴；旋转轴；对称轴；轴线；（政治）轴心；（解剖）枢椎
definition_en: an imaginary straight line around which something turns, or along which positions are measured
core_image: 一只轮子绕着中间一根看不见的杆转，杆的两端不动，轮缘上每一点都画着圆
scene: 车间里，一只砂轮固定在支架上，通电后绕着中间的杆平稳旋转。The wheel spins around a fixed axis running through its centre.
sceneCN: 这里 axis 指「物体绕之旋转的那条直线」（第 2 个义项：旋转轴）；句意：这只轮子绕着穿过圆心的固定轴旋转。图中可辨识物件：砂轮、支架、中心杆、旋转轨迹。

pos.zh: 轴线；（政治）轴心；（解剖）枢椎

senses.title: A coordinate line on a chart
senses.definition: one of the fixed reference lines, usually horizontal or vertical, along which positions and values are measured
senses.definitionCN: 固定的参考线之一，通常为水平或竖直，用来量取位置与数值
senses.example: The temperature is read from the vertical axis.
senses.exampleCN: 温度从竖直的那条轴读出。
senses.why: An axis is the fixed line against which motion or position is measured, and a chart simply draws that line on paper.
senses.whyCN: 轴是量取运动或位置的固定线，图表只是把这条线画到纸上。

senses.title: The line a body turns around
senses.definition: the straight line through a rotating body about which every point moves in a circle
senses.definitionCN: 穿过旋转物体的直线，物体上每一点都绕它作圆周运动
senses.example: The earth turns on an axis tilted about twenty-three degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 地球绕一条倾斜约二十三度的轴自转。
senses.why: Latin axis meant an axle, the physical rod a wheel turns on, and rotation is still the core image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 axis 本指车轴，即轮子绕之转动的实心杆，旋转至今仍是核心意象。

senses.title: The line that mirrors a shape
senses.definition: a line through a figure such that one half is the mirror image of the other
senses.definitionCN: 穿过图形的线，线两侧互为镜像
senses.example: A circle has an axis of symmetry in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 圆在任何方向上都有一条对称轴。
senses.why: Mirroring is a kind of turning around a fixed line, so the axle image carries over to symmetry.
senses.whyCN: 镜像对称是一种绕固定线的翻转，车轴的意象因此延伸到对称。

senses.title: A political alignment or bloc
senses.definition: a partnership or alliance between powers, especially the wartime Axis, or a line of alignment in politics
senses.definitionCN: 大国之间的结盟，尤指战时的轴心国，也指政治上的立场阵线
senses.example: Historians use the Axis for the wartime alliance of Germany and Italy.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家用「轴心」指德国与意大利的战时同盟。
senses.why: A line joining two poles gave diplomacy a word for two powers tied together around a common centre.
senses.whyCN: 连接两极的一条线，给外交提供了一个词，表示围绕共同中心绑在一起的两个强国。

senses.title: The second bone of the neck
senses.definition: the second cervical vertebra, on which the first vertebra and the head turn
senses.definitionCN: 第二块颈椎，第一颈椎与头部在它上面转动
senses.example: The axis lets the head rotate from side to side.
senses.exampleCN: 枢椎让头部左右转动。
senses.why: An anatomist named the vertebra that the head pivots on after the axle that a wheel pivots on.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学家把头部绕之转动的椎骨，按轮子绕之转动的车轴来命名。

senses.title: The long line of a structure
senses.definition: the main or longest line along which a body, organ or building is laid out
senses.definitionCN: 身体、器官或建筑沿之展开的主线或最长线
senses.example: The long axis of the bone runs from shoulder to wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 这块骨的长轴从肩延伸到腕。
senses.why: Structures grow along a dominant direction, and that direction is pictured as the axle of the form.
senses.whyCN: 结构沿一个主导方向生长，这个方向就被想象成形体的车轴。

senses.title: The centre line of a lens
senses.definition: the straight line through the centre of a lens or mirror, along which light travels without bending
senses.definitionCN: 穿过透镜或反射镜中心的直线，沿它传播的光不发生偏折
senses.example: Light along the optical axis passes straight through.
senses.exampleCN: 沿光轴传播的光直接穿过。
senses.why: Optics needs one reference line through the centre, and the old axle word is the natural name for it.
senses.whyCN: 光学需要一条穿过中心的参考线，古老的车轴词自然是它的名字。

senses.title: The central line of a solid
senses.definition: the straight line through the centre of a cylinder, cone or sphere about which the solid is generated or measured
senses.definitionCN: 穿过圆柱、圆锥或球体中心的直线，几何体绕它生成或按它测量
senses.example: A cylinder is generated by rotating a rectangle about its axis.
senses.exampleCN: 圆柱由矩形绕其轴旋转生成。
senses.why: The geometric definition keeps the original picture of rotation around a central rod.
senses.whyCN: 几何定义保留着绕中心杆旋转的原始图景。

intro.en: Axis is Latin axis 'axle, axis', which English adopted in the fourteenth century. The word has kept the physical axle at its centre through coordinate geometry, anatomy and politics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: axis 是拉丁 axis「车轴、轴」，英语十四世纪引入。经过坐标几何、解剖学与政治用法，这个词始终把实体的车轴留在中心。年代均为约数。

items.en: Axis meant the axle of a wheel, the fixed rod around which the wheel turns; the abstract line grew out of that solid object.
items.cn: axis 指车轮的车轴，即轮子绕之转动的固定杆；抽象的线正是从这件实物长出来的。

items.en: Axialis meant 'of an axis', and English axial still describes anything lying along or turning about an axis.
items.cn: axialis 意为「轴的」，英语 axial 至今形容沿轴或绕轴的事物。

items.en: English borrowed axis from Latin for the axle and for the imaginary line of a rotating body; the plural kept the Latin form axes.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪从拉丁语借入 axis，用于车轴与旋转体的假想线；复数保留了拉丁形式 axes。

items.en: The coordinate system of the seventeenth century turned the axis into a measuring line on paper, producing the modern x-axis and y-axis.
items.cn: 十七世纪的坐标系把轴变成纸上的量线，于是出现现代意义上的横轴与纵轴。

items.en: Anatomists named the pivoting vertebra the axis, and twentieth-century diplomacy used the same word for a bloc of powers.
items.cn: 解剖学家把供头部转动的椎骨命名为枢椎，二十世纪外交又用同一个词指强国阵营。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin axis, attested in the classical language, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact date of its first English use is not recorded. The older Indo-European shape is reconstructed rather than attested, and the reconstruction is offered as a form, not as a demonstrated word.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 axis，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的确切年代没有记录。更早的印欧语形态属于重构而非有据可查，该形式只是重构，并非已证实的词。

note.en: Group one holds axle words that look or sound like axis, some genuinely cognate and some unrelated; group two holds other names for a central line.
note.cn: 第一组是与 axis 形近或音近的「轴」类词，有的真同源，有的无关；第二组是中心线的其他名称。

entries.definition: The rod on which a wheel turns; it comes from Old Norse rather than Latin but shares the same ancient root.
entries.definitionCN: 轮子绕之转动的杆；来自古诺尔斯语而非拉丁语，但共享同一古老词根。

entries.definition: Lying along or turning about an axis; it is the regular adjective built from this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 沿轴或绕轴的；由这个名词构成的常规形容词。

entries.definition: The angle between a leaf and a stem; it comes from Latin ala 'wing' and has no connection with axis.
entries.definitionCN: 叶与茎之间的夹角；出自拉丁 ala「翼」，与 axis 无关。

entries.definition: The long fibre of a nerve cell; Greek axōn 'axis' is a cousin of the Latin word, not a derivative of it.
entries.definitionCN: 神经细胞的长纤维；希腊 axōn「轴」是拉丁词的远亲，并非其派生。

entries.definition: The central point or pin on which something turns; a point rather than a full line.
entries.definitionCN: 某物绕之转动的中心点或销轴；是点而非整条线。

entries.definition: A rotating rod that holds work in a machine; it is a physical shaft, close to the original axle sense.
entries.definitionCN: 机床中夹持工件的旋转杆；是实体轴，接近最初的车轴义。

entries.definition: A line running through the middle of a shape or route; it marks position without implying rotation.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过形状或路线中间的线；标出位置，但不暗示旋转。

entries.definition: The point on which a lever rests or turns; a support point, not an axis of a body.
entries.definitionCN: 杠杆搁置或转动的点；是支撑点，不是物体的轴。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin axle, the rotating wheel and the real chart, anatomy and political uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的车轴、旋转的轮子，以及真实的图表、解剖与政治用法。

normal.en: Latin axis is an axle: the wheel turns, the rod stays still.
normal.cn: 拉丁 axis 就是车轴：轮子转，杆不动。

normal.en: The plural is axes, the Latin plural, so it looks like the plural of axe.
normal.cn: 复数是 axes，拉丁复数形式，看起来像 axe 的复数。

normal.en: Charts read values along the x-axis and the y-axis.
normal.cn: 图表沿横轴与纵轴读取数值。

normal.en: The head turns on the second vertebra, called the axis.
normal.cn: 头绕第二颈椎转动，那块椎骨就叫枢椎。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: axis of rotation, axis of symmetry, optical axis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：旋转轴、对称轴、光轴。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel whose rim traces a circle while the centre stays still.
abstract.cn: 想象轮缘画出圆圈，而中心始终不动。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet folding along a crease so the two halves match.
abstract.cn: 想象纸沿一道折痕对折，两半完全吻合。

abstract.en: Picture two capitals tied by one line drawn across a map.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一条线把两个首都连在一起。

examples.en: Plot time on the horizontal axis and temperature on the vertical one.
examples.cn: 把时间画在横轴，把温度画在纵轴。

examples.en: The telescope must stay aligned with the optical axis of the mirror.
examples.cn: 望远镜必须与反射镜的光轴保持对齐。

examples.en: A biaxial crystal has two axes along which light behaves differently.
examples.cn: 双轴晶体有两条光行为不同的轴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「axis（轴）」——轮子绕它转的那根杆：轴、坐标轴

root: 拉丁 axis「车轴、轴」；形容词 axialis 衍生英语 axial。复数保留拉丁形式 axes。更早的印欧语形态属重构形式。同源远亲有希腊 axōn（轴）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses stay on one fixed line: a chart axis, a rotation axis, a mirror line, a political bloc, a pivoting vertebra, the long line of a structure, an optical centre line and the central line of a geometric solid.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都守着同一条固定线：图表坐标轴、旋转轴、镜像对称轴、政治阵营、供头转动的椎骨、结构长轴、光学中心线，以及几何体的中心轴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fixed rod through the centre, while everything around it turns or is measured against it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根穿过中心的固定杆，周围的事物绕着它转或依它量取。

chain: THE CENTRAL LINE OF A FORM

branches.en: THE GEOMETRIC LINE: a measured reference on paper and the central line of a solid are the same axle seen flat and seen solid.
branches.cn: 几何的线：纸上的量线与几何体的中心线，是同一根车轴的平面版与立体版。

branches.en: ALIGNMENT: a wheel turning and light passing straight through both depend on one central line of symmetry.
branches.cn: 对齐：轮子转动与光直穿而过，都依赖同一条中心对称线。

branches.en: MIRRORING: folding a shape about a line is rotation in reverse, so symmetry inherits the axle.
branches.cn: 镜像：沿一条线把图形折过去，是反向的旋转，对称因此继承了车轴。

branches.en: A LINE BETWEEN POWERS: diplomacy draws a line joining two poles and calls the pair an axis.
branches.cn: 强国之间的连线：外交把连接两极的线画出来，并把这一对称为轴心。

branches.en: THE BODY'S OWN AXLES: the head pivots on one vertebra, and limbs and organs grow along a long axis.
branches.cn: 身体自带的轴：头绕一块椎骨转动，四肢与器官沿长轴生长。

intro.en: Axis is a Latin noun with a small family of English adjectives and compounds; the plural axes keeps the Latin ending.
intro.cn: axis 是一个拉丁名词，带一小族英语形容词与复合词；复数 axes 保留了拉丁词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin axis 'axle' gives axialis 'of an axis'; English builds coaxial, biaxial and uniaxial by adding counting and joint prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 axis「车轴」衍生 axialis「轴的」；英语再加「共同」「二」「单」等前缀，造出同轴、双轴与单轴。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是整族词的基底。

items.example: The two axes cross at the origin.
items.exampleCN: 两条轴在原点相交。

items.example: The axial load presses along the centre.
items.exampleCN: 轴向载荷沿中心方向压下来。

items.example: The pipe expands axially when heated.
items.exampleCN: 管子受热时沿轴向膨胀。

items.example: The design balances axiality and width.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计在轴向性与宽度之间取平衡。

items.example: Coaxial cable keeps the signal inside a shield.
items.exampleCN: 同轴电缆把信号保持在屏蔽层内。

items.example: A biaxial crystal splits light in two directions.
items.exampleCN: 双轴晶体把光分成两个方向。

items.example: The uniaxial test pulls the sample in one direction.
items.exampleCN: 单轴试验只朝一个方向拉伸试样。

items.meaning: the axis-like fibre of a nerve
items.example: The axon carries signals away from the cell body.
items.exampleCN: 轴突把信号从细胞体传出去。

items.example: An axonometric drawing shows three sides at once.
items.exampleCN: 轴测图能同时显示三个面。

definition_zh: 多维的；多方面的；多元的；多维度的
definition_en: existing in or involving several dimensions, or having many different aspects rather than a single one
core_image: 一个立方体里再叠着几个方向，每个方向都能单独拉出一条刻度
scene: 投影幕上出现一个立方体，三个方向都标着刻度，旁边还叠着几张不同层面的数据表。The study treats poverty as a multidimensional problem rather than a single income figure.
sceneCN: 这里 multidimensional 指「包含许多方面、不能化成一个指标」（第 2 个义项：多方面的）；句意：这项研究把贫困当作一个多维度的问题，而不是单一收入数字。图中可辨识物件：投影幕、立方体、三条刻度轴、分层数据表。

pos.zh: 多维的；多方面的；多元的

derivatives.zh: 多维分析（数据分析方法）

senses.title: Having several spatial dimensions
senses.definition: described by more than three coordinates, as a mathematical or physical space can be
senses.definitionCN: 用三个以上坐标来描述，数学或物理空间可以如此
senses.example: The dataset lives in a multidimensional space of ten coordinates.
senses.exampleCN: 这个数据集处在一个十坐标的多维空间里。
senses.why: Multi- 'many' plus dimension: space itself can be given more axes than the three of ordinary experience.
senses.whyCN: multi-「多」加 dimension：空间可以比日常经验的三维多出更多轴。

senses.title: Having many aspects
senses.definition: involving several distinct factors or sides that cannot be reduced to one measure
senses.definitionCN: 涉及几个不同因素或侧面，不能简化成一个指标
senses.example: Housing is a multidimensional issue of cost, safety and location.
senses.exampleCN: 住房是涉及成本、安全与位置的多方面问题。
senses.why: A single number is one dimension; when a problem needs several numbers at once, it becomes multidimensional.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字就是一维；一个问题需要同时用几个数字衡量，就变成多维的。

senses.title: An array with several indices
senses.definition: a data structure whose elements are addressed by two or more indices, such as a table or a cube
senses.definitionCN: 元素由两个或更多下标定位的数据结构，如表格或数据立方
senses.example: The image is stored as a multidimensional array of pixel values.
senses.exampleCN: 图像被存成一个由像素值构成的多维数组。
senses.why: Each index adds an axis, so a table of tables is literally an array with more than one dimension.
senses.whyCN: 每增加一个下标就多一条轴，因此「表格的表格」字面上就是多维数组。

senses.title: Mapping distances into fewer axes
senses.titleCN: 把距离压缩到较少坐标上
senses.definition: a statistical technique that places objects in a low-dimensional map while preserving their measured distances
senses.definitionCN: 把对象放到低维图上、同时尽量保留其测得距离的统计方法
senses.example: Multidimensional scaling turned the survey distances into a two-axis map.
senses.exampleCN: 多维标度法把调查得到的距离转成一张两轴图。
senses.why: The method takes many measured dimensions and squeezes them into a few axes that can be drawn.
senses.whyCN: 这种方法把许多测得的维度压缩成几条可以画出来的轴。

senses.title: Analysis across several attributes
senses.definition: querying and summarising data by several attributes at once, as in a data warehouse cube
senses.definitionCN: 同时按多个属性查询与汇总数据，如数据仓库中的立方体
senses.example: The sales team ran a multidimensional analysis by region and quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 销售团队按地区与季度做了一次多维分析。
senses.why: Each attribute is an axis of the cube, so slicing by two attributes is a multidimensional operation.
senses.whyCN: 每个属性都是立方体的一条轴，按两个属性切分就是多维操作。

senses.title: A person with many sides
senses.definition: having a rich and varied character, identity or talent rather than a single flat trait
senses.definitionCN: 性格、身份或才能丰富多样，而不是单一扁平的特质
senses.example: The portrait presents a multidimensional character, not a hero or a villain.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅人物画像呈现一个有多个侧面的人物，而非简单的英雄或恶人。
senses.why: Describing a person in more than one dimension is the same metaphor as describing a space with more than one axis.
senses.whyCN: 用不止一个维度来描述人，与用不止一条轴描述空间，是同一个比喻。

senses.title: Poverty measured on several scales
senses.titleCN: 用多个尺度衡量的贫困
senses.definition: an index that counts deprivations in health, education and living standards together rather than income alone
senses.definitionCN: 把健康、教育与生活水平方面的匮乏合并计算，而非只看收入的指数
senses.example: The multidimensional poverty index counts several deprivations at once.
senses.exampleCN: 多维贫困指数同时计算多项匮乏。
senses.why: Poverty has more than one face, so the measure adds axes instead of collapsing everything into income.
senses.whyCN: 贫困不止一副面孔，因此这种测量增加坐标轴，而不是把所有东西压成收入一项。

senses.title: Extra dimensions in modern physics
senses.titleCN: 现代物理中的额外维度
senses.definition: describing theories in which space has more than the three familiar dimensions, often compactified and unseen
senses.definitionCN: 描述空间多于熟悉的三维、额外维度常被紧致化而不可见的理论
senses.example: String theory requires a multidimensional universe with hidden extra dimensions.
senses.exampleCN: 弦理论需要一个带隐藏额外维度的多维宇宙。
senses.why: Physics extends the geometric meaning to dimensions that exist mathematically even when they cannot be seen.
senses.whyCN: 物理把几何义扩展到那些数学上存在、却看不见的维度。

intro.en: Multidimensional is an English compound of multi- 'many', from Latin multus, and dimension, from Latin dimensio 'a measuring', built on dimetiri 'to measure out'. The compound itself is modern English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: multidimensional 是英语复合词，由 multi-「多」（出自拉丁 multus）与 dimension（出自拉丁 dimensio「测量」，由 dimetiri「量出」构成）组成。复合词本身属现代英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Multus meant 'much, many', and it gives English multi-, multitude and multiply; it supplies the 'many' of the compound.
items.cn: multus 意为「多、许多」，衍生英语 multi-、multitude 与 multiply；它为复合词提供了「多」这一部分。

items.en: Metiri meant 'to measure', and it also gives meter and measure; measuring is the older core of dimension.
items.cn: metiri 意为「测量」，也衍生 meter 与 measure；测量是 dimension 更古老的核心。

items.en: Dimensio was 'a measuring out'; English dimension first meant a measurement and later a direction in which a body extends.
items.cn: dimensio 意为「量出」；英语 dimension 先指测量，后指物体延伸的一个方向。

items.en: English joined multi- and dimensional to describe spaces, data and problems that need more than one axis.
items.cn: 英语把 multi- 与 dimensional 拼在一起，描述需要不止一条轴的空间、数据与问题。

items.en: Multidimensional scaling, multidimensional arrays and multidimensional analysis each fixed a technical sense in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 多维标度法、多维数组与多维分析都在二十世纪固定了各自的技术含义。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the word is a transparent English compound of multi- and dimensional, so its formation is not in doubt; only the earliest recorded English use is undated. The deeper origin of multus is not established, and no reconstructed root is asserted.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：这个词是 multi- 与 dimensional 构成的透明英语复合词，构词方式并不存疑；只是英语最早用例没有确切年代。multus 的更早来源无定论，此处不给出重构词根。

note.en: Group one shares the dimension stock, where a suffix or prefix changes how many axes are being counted; group two holds words for many-sided things that are not strictly geometric.
note.cn: 第一组共享 dimension 词干，前后缀改变的是「数几条轴」；第二组是形容多面事物、但不严格属于几何的词。

entries.definition: A single measurable direction or aspect; multidimensional simply multiplies it.
entries.definitionCN: 一条可测量的方向或一个方面；multidimensional 只是把它变成多条。

entries.definition: Relating to dimensions; multi- attaches to this adjective to make the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 与维度有关的；multi- 加在这个形容词上构成复合词。

entries.definition: The state of having several dimensions; the abstract noun built from the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 具有多个维度的状态；由该形容词构成的名词。

entries.definition: Measured or understood along a single axis; the direct opposite of multidimensional.
entries.definitionCN: 只沿一条轴测量或理解；与 multidimensional 直接相对。

entries.definition: Having many sides or aspects, often of a person or a problem; the picture is a cut gem, not a coordinate space.
entries.definitionCN: 有许多侧面或方面，常用于人或问题；意象是切面宝石，而非坐标空间。

entries.definition: Involving several measured variables; a statistical term close to multidimensional analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及多个被测变量；接近多维分析的统计术语。

entries.definition: Having many aspects; the everyday phrase with no technical definition.
entries.definitionCN: 有许多方面；没有技术定义的日常说法。

entries.definition: Made of many connected parts; it stresses difficulty of understanding rather than number of axes.
entries.definitionCN: 由许多相互关联的部分组成；强调理解的难度，而非轴的数目。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: Latin 'many' plus Latin 'measure', the array with several indices and the real statistical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「多」加拉丁「测量」、带多个下标的数组，以及真实的统计用法。

normal.en: Multi- 'many' plus dimension: more than one axis.
normal.cn: multi-「多」加 dimension：不止一条轴。

normal.en: A table has two indices, so it is already multidimensional.
normal.cn: 一张表有两个下标，本身就已经是多维的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: multidimensional array, multidimensional scaling, multidimensional analysis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：多维数组、多维标度法、多维分析。

normal.en: The opposite is unidimensional, built with the prefix meaning one.
normal.cn: 反义是 unidimensional，用表示「一」的前缀构成。

normal.en: Development studies count several deprivations together as multidimensional poverty.
normal.cn: 发展研究把多项匮乏合并计算，称为多维贫困。

abstract.en: Picture a cube with a second set of axes growing out of each corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一个立方体的每个角上又长出一组新的轴。

abstract.en: Picture a problem that cannot be written on one line of a form.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题没法填进表格的一行里。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait painted from several directions at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅同时从几个方向画成的人像。

examples.en: The sensor produces a multidimensional signal that must be reduced before plotting.
examples.cn: 传感器产生多维信号，绘图前必须先降维。

examples.en: A multidimensional approach to health considers diet, housing and income together.
examples.cn: 对健康的多维研究把饮食、住房与收入放在一起考虑。

examples.en: The team used multidimensional scaling to place the samples on a simple map.
examples.cn: 团队用多维标度法把样本放到一张简单的地图上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「multi（多）+ dimensional（维度的）」——有很多个维度：多维的、多方面的

root: 英语复合词：multi-（拉丁 multus「多」）+ dimensional（dimension 出自拉丁 dimensio「测量」，源于 dimetiri「量出」）。复合本身是英语构词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses add axes one by one: a many-coordinate space, a problem with many aspects, an array with several indices, a distance map, analysis across attributes, a many-sided person, a poverty index and unseen dimensions in physics.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项一条条加上轴：多坐标空间、包含多方面的问题、带多个下标的数组、距离映射、跨属性分析、有多个侧面的人、贫困指数，以及物理中看不见的维度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more axis added to the familiar three, so that no single number can describe the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：在熟悉的三维之外再加一条轴，于是没有任何一个数字能描述整体。

branches.en: GEOMETRIC AXES: an ordinary many-coordinate space and the hidden dimensions of physics are the same geometry at different scales of belief.
branches.cn: 几何的轴：寻常的多坐标空间与物理中隐藏的维度，是同一几何在不同可信尺度上的样子。

branches.en: MANY SIDES: a problem and a person both resist being reduced to one measurement.
branches.cn: 多个侧面：一个问题与一个人，都不肯被压成一个测量值。

branches.en: DATA CUBES: an array with several indices and an analysis across attributes are the storage and the query of the same cube.
branches.cn: 数据立方：带多个下标的数组与跨属性分析，是同一个立方体的存储面与查询面。

branches.en: THE DISTANCE MAP: scaling squeezes many measured axes into a few that can be drawn.
branches.cn: 距离地图：标度法把许多测得的轴压成少数几条可以画出来的轴。

branches.en: COUNTING DEPRIVATIONS: poverty is measured on several scales because one scale hides the rest.
branches.cn: 清点匮乏：贫困要用多个尺度衡量，因为单一尺度会把其余的都遮住。

intro.en: Multidimensional combines a Latin quantity prefix with an English adjective that Latin built from a measuring verb.
intro.cn: multidimensional 把拉丁数量前缀与一个英语形容词组合起来，而那个形容词由拉丁测量动词构成。

latinIntro.en: Multus 'many' gives multi- and multiply; metiri 'to measure' gives meter, measure and dimensio; -alis survives as -al in dimensional.
latinIntro.cn: multus「多」衍生 multi- 与 multiply；metiri「测量」衍生 meter、measure 与 dimensio；-alis 在 dimensional 中留下 -al。

items.example: Multi- turns a single-axis adjective into a many-axis one.
items.exampleCN: multi- 把单轴形容词变成多轴形容词。

items.example: The Latin adjective is the source of the prefix.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词是前缀的来源。

items.example: The verb supplies the measuring inside dimension.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 dimension 内部的「测量」义。

items.example: The Latin noun became English dimension.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词变成英语 dimension。

items.example: A line has one dimension and a cube has three.
items.exampleCN: 线有一维，立方体有三元。

items.example: The model is three-dimensional.
items.exampleCN: 这个模型是三维的。

items.example: The table stores a multidimensional array.
items.exampleCN: 这张表存着一个多维数组。
