definition_zh: 精确；精密度；精确性；（仪器、测量的）精度；有效数字位数；（加工）公差
definition_en: the quality of being exact, especially the fineness of a measurement or the closeness of repeated readings to one another
core_image: 一把薄刃把多余的部分削掉，只留下真正要的那一点
scene: 实验室的台面上摆着一支滴定管、一本记录册和一台电子天平，同一份样品被反复称了五回。The precision of the balance showed in five readings that differed by less than a milligram.
sceneCN: 这里 precision 指「统计意义上的重复一致性」（第 2 个义项：重复测量的一致程度）；句意：这台天平的精密度体现在五次读数相差不到一毫克。图中可辨识物件：滴定管、记录册、电子天平、样品瓶。

pos.zh: 精确；精密度；精度；精确性

senses.title: The fineness of a stated measurement
senses.titleCN: 测量值本身的精细程度
senses.definition: the degree to which a stated measurement is divided into fine enough steps for two nearby values to be told apart
senses.definitionCN: 一个测量值被细分到多细的程度，即能否把两个接近的值区分开
senses.example: The precision of the reading was limited by the smallest mark on the ruler.
senses.exampleCN: 这个读数的精度受限于尺子上最小的那道刻度。
senses.why: Praecisio is a cutting off, and a finely stated measurement is one cut into narrow slices.
senses.whyCN: praecisio 本义是切去，精细报出的测量值就是把量切成一薄片一薄片。

senses.title: Repeatability across repeated measurements
senses.definition: in statistics, the closeness of repeated measurements to one another, whether or not they sit near the true value
senses.definitionCN: 统计上多次测量彼此接近的程度，与它们是否靠近真值无关
senses.example: The five runs showed high precision even when the average was slightly off.
senses.exampleCN: 五次运行即使平均值略有偏差，重复精密度依然很高。
senses.why: Statistics separates the scatter among repeats, called precision, from the distance to the truth, called accuracy.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把重复测量的分散程度称为精密度，把与真值的距离称为准确度，两者分开。

senses.title: The smallest step an instrument can show
senses.definition: the smallest change in a quantity that an instrument can register, display or resolve
senses.definitionCN: 仪器能够记录、显示或分辨的最小变化量
senses.example: The instrument's precision reaches one part in a million.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器的精度达到百万分之一。
senses.why: An instrument whose scale is cut more finely can separate values that a coarse one merges.
senses.whyCN: 刻度切得更细的仪器，能把粗仪器混在一起的值分开。

senses.title: Exactness in wording
senses.definition: careful exactness in the choice of words, so that a statement admits only one reading
senses.definitionCN: 用词上的细致准确，使一句话只容许一种读法
senses.example: She described the procedure with the precision of a manual.
senses.exampleCN: 她像操作手册一样精确地描述了步骤。
senses.why: Latin praecisio also meant brevity of speech, where every surplus word has been cut away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecisio 也指言辞简省，即把多余的词都切掉。

senses.title: Targeted action on a small site
senses.titleCN: 精准农业与精准医疗的定点干预
senses.definition: an approach that directs water, treatment or medicine only to the exact field, place or patient that needs it
senses.definitionCN: 只把水、处理或药物投到确切需要的田块、地点或病人身上的做法
senses.example: Precision irrigation delivers water to the driest rows alone.
senses.exampleCN: 精准灌溉只把水送到最干的那几垄。
senses.why: The modern compounds keep the old image of a cut made exactly where it is wanted.
senses.whyCN: 现代复合词保留了老意象：只在需要的地方下刀。

senses.title: The number of reliable digits
senses.definition: the count of digits in a reported value that carry real information about how finely it is known
senses.definitionCN: 一个报告值中携带真实精细信息的数字位数
senses.example: Report the mean to four digits of precision.
senses.exampleCN: 把平均值报到四位有效数字。
senses.why: Digits past the reliable cut are noise, so counting the trustworthy digits states the precision.
senses.whyCN: 可靠切点之后的位只是噪声，数出可信位数就是在说明精度。

senses.title: Machining to a very small tolerance
senses.titleCN: 机械加工的公差与精度
senses.definition: the closeness with which a machined part matches its specified size, measured in very small units
senses.definitionCN: 加工件与规定尺寸吻合的紧密程度，以极小的单位计量
senses.example: The shop grinds bearings to a precision of two microns.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把轴承磨到两微米的精度。
senses.why: In a machine shop the abstract fineness becomes metal cut away until the part fits.
senses.whyCN: 在机加工车间，抽象的精细变成被切掉的金属，直到零件合适。

senses.title: Strict exactness in legal or formal form
senses.titleCN: 法律或形式上的严格精确
senses.definition: the strict following of exact wording or procedure, where no looseness or paraphrase is permitted
senses.definitionCN: 严格遵循确切的措辞或程序，不允许任何松动或改写
senses.example: The clause was drafted with precision to close every loophole.
senses.exampleCN: 这一条款起草得十分精确，堵住了每个漏洞。
senses.why: A legal cut must fall on exactly the right word, which is the original image applied to text.
senses.whyCN: 法律之刀必须落在确切的字上，正是原意象用在文本上。

intro.en: Precision comes from Latin praecisio 'a cutting off', a noun of action from praecidere 'to cut short', built on prae- 'in front' plus caedere 'to cut'. French carried the word into English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: precision 出自拉丁 praecisio「切去」，是 praecidere「切短」的动作名词，由 prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」构成。英语十六世纪经法语引入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caedere meant 'to cut, to strike down'; it also underlies incision, excise and decision, each of which turns on a cut.
items.cn: caedere 意为「切、砍倒」，也构成 incision、excise 与 decision，这几个词都围绕「切」展开。

items.en: Prae- 'in front' plus caedere made praecidere 'to cut off in front, to shorten'; a speech that was praecisus had its surplus trimmed away.
items.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere 构成 praecidere「切去前面、截短」；被称作 praecisus 的言辞就是把多余部分削掉了。

items.en: Praecisio named the act of cutting off and also brevity of style, so the notion of fine trimming sits inside both senses.
items.cn: praecisio 既指切去的动作，也指文风的简省，因此「削到恰好」的观念同时存在于这两层。

items.en: Middle French precision brought the word into English, first for concise speech and only later for exact measurement.
items.cn: 中古法语 precision 把这个词带进英语，先用于简练的言辞，较晚才用于精确测量。

items.en: Nineteenth-century science and manufacturing applied the word to instrument scales and machined parts, which produced the modern technical senses.
items.cn: 十九世纪的科学与制造业把这个词用到仪器刻度和加工零件上，现代技术义项由此形成。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin praecisio, attested in the classical language, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact year of its first English use is not recorded. The usual route is through French, while a direct Latin borrowing is also argued; no single route is imposed here.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 praecisio，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的具体年份没有记录。通常认为经法语传入，也有直接借自拉丁语的说法；此处不强行选定单一传入路径。

note.en: Group one is the same Latin family seen through its adjective, adverb and negative forms; group two holds the measuring partners that share the field but answer a different question.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族在形容词、副词与否定形式上的样子；第二组是同处测量领域的伙伴词，但它们回答的是另一个问题。

entries.definition: Giving exact details with nothing vague; it describes the thing or the person, while precision names the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 给出确切细节、毫不含糊；它形容事物或人，而 precision 是这种性质本身。

entries.definition: In an exact way, or used as an emphatic 'exactly'; it modifies an action rather than naming a measured degree.
entries.definitionCN: 以确切的方式，或用作加强语气的「正是」；它修饰动作，不指一个测得的程度。

entries.definition: Lack of exactness, formed with the negative prefix im-; it is the direct opposite of precision in every sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不精确，由否定前缀 im- 构成；在各义项上都是 precision 的反面。

entries.definition: A less common synonym for precision, stressing the manner of being exact rather than a measured degree of fineness.
entries.definitionCN: precision 的罕用同义词，强调一丝不苟的作风，而非测得的精细程度。

entries.definition: How near a measurement lies to the true value; a rifle can be accurate while its shots are widely spread.
entries.definitionCN: 测量值与真值的接近程度；一支枪可以很准确，但弹着点散布很广。

entries.definition: The state of being wholly correct, often said of a figure or a copy rather than of a spread of repeats.
entries.definitionCN: 完全正确的状态，常用于数字或副本，而不是重复测量的散布。

entries.definition: The smallest interval an instrument or an image can distinguish; it is the hardware side of precision.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器或图像能分辨的最小间隔；它是精密度在硬件上的表现。

entries.definition: The range of variation a specification allows; precision is the aim, tolerance is the slack accepted around it.
entries.definitionCN: 规格允许的变动范围；precision 是瞄准的目标，tolerance 是允许的松量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin cut, the fine scale and the fixed phrases that keep the word technical.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的「切」、细密的刻度，以及把这个词固定在技术语境里的搭配。

normal.en: Prae- 'before' plus caedere 'to cut': trim off the surplus.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」：把多余的部分削掉。

normal.en: A fine scale cuts a quantity into narrow slices.
normal.cn: 细密的刻度把一个量切成一薄片一薄片。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: precision measurement, precision instrument, precision farming.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：精密测量、精密仪器、精准农业。

normal.en: Statistics keeps precision for repeats and accuracy for the true value.
normal.cn: 统计学用「精密度」说重复，用「准确度」说真值。

normal.en: In a machine shop precision is measured in microns.
normal.cn: 在机加工车间，精度以微米计。

abstract.en: Picture a blade shaving a hair's width off a metal block.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃从金属块上削下一根头发那么薄的一层。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose marks sit closer together than a fingernail.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，刻度线比指甲还窄。

abstract.en: Picture five arrows in one tight cluster, though none of them near the bullseye.
abstract.cn: 想象五支箭扎在同一小簇里，却都不靠近靶心。

examples.en: The survey reported its margin with more precision than the sample size deserved.
examples.cn: 这项调查报出的误差范围，比它的样本量所能支撑的更为精细。

examples.en: Precision alone does not make a scale trustworthy if it was zeroed wrongly.
examples.cn: 如果零点调错了，光有精密度并不能让一台秤可信。

examples.en: Precision medicine matches a drug to the genetic profile of one patient.
examples.cn: 精准医疗把药物匹配到某一位病人的基因特征上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre（在前）+ cise（切）」——把多余的部分切掉，留下的就是精确

root: 拉丁 praecisio「切去」= praecidere（prae-「在前」+ caedere「切」）的动作名词。同族词有 precise、precisely、preciseness、imprecision。英语经法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one cut: a finely stated value, statistical repeatability, an instrument's smallest step, exact wording, targeted action, reliable digits, machining tolerance and strict legal form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守着同一刀：精细报出的测量值、统计上的重复一致性、仪器的最小刻度、确切的措辞、定点干预、可靠位数、加工公差，以及法律形式上的严格精确。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin blade cutting away everything that is not the exact point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把薄刃削掉一切不属于那一点的部分。

branches.en: FINE DIVISIONS: stating a value in narrow steps and counting the reliable digits are the same cut seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 细分：把值报成窄小的台阶与数出可靠位数，是同一刀的两面。

branches.en: REPEATS AGREE: statistical precision is the spread among repeats, not the distance from the truth.
branches.cn: 重复一致：统计上的精密度是重复测量之间的散布，而不是与真值的距离。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT'S EDGE: a finer scale lets a device separate what a coarse one merges.
branches.cn: 仪器的刃口：刻度更细的装置能把粗装置混在一起的值分开。

branches.en: CLEAN WORDING: exact speech and strict legal form both cut off every second reading.
branches.cn: 干净的措辞：确切的表达与严格的法律形式，都切掉了第二种读法。

branches.en: ACTION AT ONE SPOT: precision farming and precision machining both demand the cut land where the work requires.
branches.cn: 定点下手：精准农业与精密加工都要求这一刀落在工作真正需要的地方。

intro.en: Precision is a Latin noun of action built from a prefix, a verb root and a suffix, and the same pieces also build the everyday adjectives precise and imprecise.
intro.cn: precision 是由前缀、动词词根与后缀构成的拉丁动作名词，同样的构件也造出日常形容词 precise 与 imprecise。

latinIntro.en: Prae- 'in front' plus caedere 'to cut' yields praecidere, and -io turns it into the action noun praecisio; English then adds -ly and -ness and negates the whole word with im-.
latinIntro.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」得到 praecidere，-io 把它变成动作名词 praecisio；英语再加上 -ly 与 -ness，并用 im- 否定整个词。

items.example: The prefix puts the cutting ahead of the thing cut.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把切割放在被切之物的前面。

items.example: Incision and excise share this verb.
items.exampleCN: incision 与 excise 共用这个动词。

items.example: A long speech could be cut down to a short one.
items.exampleCN: 一段长话可以被截短成几句。

items.example: The Latin noun already carried the idea of trimming to the right size.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已经含有「削到恰好」的意思。

items.example: The word moved from speech to instruments.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从言辞转到了仪器上。

items.example: A precise answer leaves no room for a second reading.
items.exampleCN: 确切的回答不给第二种读法留空间。

items.example: The parts fit precisely together.
items.exampleCN: 这些零件严丝合缝地拼在一起。

items.example: Any imprecision in the clock ruins the timing.
items.exampleCN: 时钟的任何不精确都会毁掉计时。

items.example: An imprecise word can start a quarrel.
items.exampleCN: 一个不准确的词就能引起争吵。

items.example: Her preciseness made the instructions easy to follow.
items.exampleCN: 她的一丝不苟让说明容易照着做。

definition_zh: 计算；计算过程；计算结果；（计算机）运算；计算理论；数值模拟
definition_en: the act or process of working out a result by arithmetic or by following formal rules, or the result so produced
core_image: 一长串数字排成队，被一道道规则依次处理，末端吐出一个总数
scene: 夜里机房的指示灯一直闪，一排机柜正在处理同一批气象数据，风扇声盖过了键盘声。The overnight computation turned a week of weather records into a single forecast map.
sceneCN: 这里 computation 指「计算机执行的大规模处理」（第 6 个义项：科学计算与数值模拟）；句意：夜间这次计算把一周的天气记录变成了一张预报图。图中可辨识物件：机柜、指示灯、风扇、气象数据屏。

pos.zh: 计算；计算过程；计算结果；运算

senses.title: The act of working a result out by hand
senses.definition: the act of working out an answer by arithmetic or by careful step-by-step reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 用算术或一步一步的仔细推理求出答案的动作
senses.example: By hand, the computation took three hours and many sheets of paper.
senses.exampleCN: 手工算这一回花了三个小时和许多张纸。
senses.why: Computatio named the act of reckoning together long before machines existed to do it.
senses.whyCN: 早在机器会算之前，computatio 就已经命名了「把数归拢起来清点」这个动作。

senses.title: The result that comes out
senses.definition: the answer or figure produced by working something out
senses.definitionCN: 经过推算得出的答案或数字
senses.example: Her computation was wrong in the second column.
senses.exampleCN: 她的计算结果在第二列就错了。
senses.why: A Latin noun of action could also name the thing the action produced, so the reckoning and its answer share one word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动作名词也能指动作产生之物，因此计算过程与算出的答案共用一词。

senses.title: Processing done by a machine
senses.definition: the work a computer performs when it executes instructions on data
senses.definitionCN: 计算机对数据执行指令时所做的工作
senses.example: The computation finished before the screen refreshed.
senses.exampleCN: 运算在屏幕刷新之前就完成了。
senses.why: When machines took over the reckoning, the old noun moved onto silicon without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 当机器接过清点的工作，这个老名词原封不动地搬到了硅片上。

senses.title: One run of a formal rule system
senses.titleCN: 按某种规则体系完成的一次计算
senses.definition: a single execution of a set of rules, as in a model, an automaton or one step of a proof
senses.definitionCN: 一套规则的一次执行，如模型、自动机或证明中的一步
senses.example: Each computation of the rule set produces the next state of the grid.
senses.exampleCN: 规则集的每一次计算都产生网格的下一个状态。
senses.why: A formal system replaces pebbles with rules, yet one pass through the rules is still one reckoning.
senses.whyCN: 形式系统用小石子换成了规则，但把规则走一遍仍然是一次计算。

senses.title: The theory of what can be computed
senses.titleCN: 计算理论：可计算性与复杂度
senses.definition: the branch of study concerned with which problems a procedure can solve and at what cost
senses.definitionCN: 研究一个过程能解哪些问题、代价有多大的理论分支
senses.example: Computation theory asks which problems no program can ever solve.
senses.exampleCN: 计算理论研究哪些问题是任何程序都永远解不出的。
senses.why: The noun for one reckoning became the name of the whole field that studies reckonings in general.
senses.whyCN: 一次计算的名词，变成了研究一切计算的整个领域的名称。

senses.title: Numerical simulation of physical systems
senses.definition: the use of large numerical procedures to imitate a physical process such as weather, fluid flow or a collision
senses.definitionCN: 用大型数值程序模仿天气、流体或碰撞等物理过程
senses.example: Climate forecasts depend on heavy computation run on parallel machines.
senses.exampleCN: 气候预报依赖在并行机器上运行的大规模计算。
senses.why: Simulation is reckoning pushed until the numbers behave like the system they describe.
senses.whyCN: 模拟就是把计算推到极致，直到数字表现得像它所描述的系统。

senses.title: Information processing in a brain or a cell
senses.titleCN: 大脑或细胞执行的计算
senses.definition: the transformation of information carried out by a natural system, such as a nervous system or a single cell
senses.definitionCN: 自然系统对信息所做的转换，如神经系统或单个细胞
senses.example: The brain performs a computation that turns pressure waves into understood words.
senses.exampleCN: 大脑执行一种计算，把声波变成听懂的词。
senses.why: Cognitive science borrowed the machine word to describe what nervous tissue does with signals.
senses.whyCN: 认知科学借用了机器的词，来描述神经组织对信号做了什么。

senses.title: The time and memory a procedure consumes
senses.titleCN: 计算的时间与空间代价
senses.definition: the time and storage that a procedure requires, often growing with the size of its input
senses.definitionCN: 一个过程所需的时间与存储，常随输入规模增大而增长
senses.example: The cost of a computation grows with the square of the input length.
senses.exampleCN: 一次计算的代价随输入长度的平方增长。
senses.why: Once reckoning is measured, the noun also names its price in time and memory.
senses.whyCN: 一旦清点被计量，这个名词也用来指它在时间与内存上的价格。

intro.en: Computation comes from Latin computatio 'a reckoning', a noun of action from computare 'to reckon together', built on com- 'together' plus putare. French carried the noun into English in the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: computation 出自拉丁 computatio「清点」，是 computare「一起清点」的动作名词，由 com-「一起」加 putare 构成。英语十五世纪经法语引入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Putare first meant 'to prune, to clean up' and later 'to reckon, to think'; English putative keeps the thinking side of the verb.
items.cn: putare 最初意为「修剪、清理」，后转为「清点、思考」；英语 putative 保留了「认为」这一面。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus putare gave computare 'to reckon together, to sum up'; the trimming image survives in the idea of tidying a count.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 putare 构成 computare「一起清点、合计」；把数目理顺这一想法里还留着修剪的影子。

items.en: Computatio was the action noun for the reckoning, and it could also name the written record of an account.
items.cn: computatio 是表示清点这一动作的名词，也能指账目的书面记录。

items.en: Old French computation passed the word into English in the fifteenth century, at first for arithmetic done in books and ledgers.
items.cn: 古法语 computation 在十五世纪把这个词传入英语，最初指在账簿上做的算术。

items.en: Twentieth-century computing moved the noun onto electronic processors, and later onto brains and cells treated as information machines.
items.cn: 二十世纪的计算技术把这个名词转用到电子处理器上，后来又用于被当作信息机器的大脑与细胞。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin computatio, attested in the classical language and taken through French, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact year of its first English use is not recorded. The deeper origin of putare is disputed, and no single account is imposed.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 computatio，经法语传入，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的具体年份没有记录。putare 的更早来源有争议，此处不强行选定一种说法。

note.en: Group one follows the compute verb through its agent, its adjective and its everyday cousin; group two holds neighbouring words for reckoning that differ in scope and tone.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 compute 这个动词，看它的施动者、形容词与日常近亲；第二组是相邻的「算」类词，范围与语气各不相同。

entries.definition: To work out a result, now usually by machine; computation is the noun of that act.
entries.definitionCN: 算出结果，现在通常指用机器算；computation 是这一动作的名词。

entries.definition: A device that executes instructions; the ending -er names the agent, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 执行指令的设备；词尾 -er 指施动者，不指过程。

entries.definition: Able to be produced by a procedure in a finite number of steps; a strictly technical adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 能由某个过程在有限步内产生的；是严格的技术形容词。

entries.definition: To name numbers in order or to tally items; it descends from the same Latin verb through French but stays simple.
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序数数或清点物品；经法语出自同一拉丁动词，但用法一直简单。

entries.definition: The process of working figures out by arithmetic; it stresses the steps, while computation can mean the whole run or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 用算术一步步算出数字的过程；强调步骤，而 computation 可指整次运行或其结果。

entries.definition: The branch of mathematics that deals with numbers; it names the field, not one act of reckoning.
entries.definitionCN: 研究数的数学分支；指学科，不指某一次清点。

entries.definition: An accounting or a settling of accounts, often with a moral edge that computation does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 结账或清算，常带道德意味，而 computation 没有这层色彩。

entries.definition: Handling data by a defined procedure; it covers the mechanical side without the arithmetic flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 按既定流程处理数据；涵盖机械处理的一面，不带算术气息。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin reckoning, the machine run, and the phrases that carry the word into technical writing.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的清点、机器的运行，以及把这个词带进技术写作的搭配。

normal.en: Com- 'together' plus putare 'to reckon': add the pebbles up.
normal.cn: com-「一起」加 putare「清点」：把小石子归拢起来加总。

normal.en: Putare 'to prune' turned into 'to reckon': tidying numbers into a total.
normal.cn: putare 从「修剪」转为「清点」：把数字理顺成一个总数。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: computation time, numerical computation, computation cost.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：计算时间、数值计算、计算代价。

normal.en: The same family gives compute, computer and computable.
normal.cn: 同族词给出 compute、computer 与 computable。

normal.en: One computation can be a single run or the whole field of study.
normal.cn: 一次计算既可以指一趟运行，也可以指整个研究领域。

abstract.en: Picture a hand moving pebbles from a heap into marked squares.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把小石子从堆里挪进划好格子的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a silent rack of machines turning rows of numbers overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一排无声的机器整夜翻动成行的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a cell reading a signal and writing a response.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细胞读入信号、写出回应。

examples.en: A short computation on paper settled an argument that a long debate could not.
examples.cn: 纸上一次简短的计算，解决了长久争论解决不了的问题。

examples.en: The course covers computation from hand arithmetic to parallel simulation.
examples.cn: 这门课涵盖从手工算术到并行模拟的计算。

examples.en: Biologists now ask what computation a network of neurons performs.
examples.cn: 生物学家现在会问：一片神经元网络执行的是什么样的计算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「com（一起）+ put（清点）+ ation」——把数一起清点起来：计算、运算

root: 拉丁 computatio「清点」= computare（com-「一起」+ putare「清点、修剪」）的动作名词。同族词有 compute、computer、computable、count、account。英语经法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one reckoning: the act by hand, the answer it yields, a machine run, a formal rule run, the theory of what can be computed, simulation, natural information processing and the price in time and memory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次清点：手工算的动作、得出的答案、机器的一次运行、规则体系的一次执行、可计算性理论、模拟、自然系统的信息处理，以及时间与内存的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long row of numbers passing through rules until one total drops out at the end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一长串数字穿过一道道规则，末端落出一个总数。

chain: A PRICE IN TIME AND MEMORY

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS ANSWER: the hand at work and the figure it leaves are two sides of one noun.
branches.cn: 动作与答案：劳作的手与它留下的数字，是同一个名词的两面。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF RUN: silicon and a formal rule set each complete one pass, so both count as one computation.
branches.cn: 两种运行：硅片与形式规则集各自走完一趟，都算一次计算。

branches.en: THE THEORY OF COST: what can be computed and at what price in time and memory are the two questions of the field.
branches.cn: 代价的理论：什么算得出来、要花多少时间与内存，是这个领域的两个问题。

branches.en: SIMULATION: numbers are pushed until they behave like the weather or the fluid they stand for.
branches.cn: 模拟：数字被推到表现得像它们所代表的天气或流体。

branches.en: NATURE RECKONS: a brain or a cell transforms signals, so the machine word fits living tissue.
branches.cn: 自然也在算：大脑或细胞转换信号，机器的词因此适用于活组织。

intro.en: Computation is a Latin noun built from a prefix, a verb root and two suffixes, and the same pieces build the verb, the machine and the adjective for what can be worked out.
intro.cn: computation 是由前缀、动词词根与两个后缀构成的拉丁名词，同样的构件也造出动词、机器名称与「算得出来」的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Com- 'together' plus putare 'to reckon' gives computare, -io makes the action noun computatio, and English adds -er and -able while count and account arrive through French.
latinIntro.cn: com-「一起」加 putare「清点」得到 computare，-io 构成动作名词 computatio；英语再加 -er 与 -able，而 count 与 account 经法语传入。

items.example: The prefix turns a single reckoning into a summing up.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把单独的清点变成合计。

items.example: The verb moved from cutting plants to settling numbers.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词从修剪植物转到结清数目。

items.meaning: to reckon together; to sum up
items.example: The verb is older than any machine that performs it.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词比任何执行它的机器都古老。

items.example: The Latin noun could name both the act and the record.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词既能指动作，也能指记录。

items.example: The computation ran all night.
items.exampleCN: 这次计算跑了一整夜。

items.example: Programs compute the answer in seconds.
items.exampleCN: 程序几秒钟就算出答案。

items.example: The suffix marks the doer of the reckoning.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记执行计算的施动者。

items.example: Not every well-defined function is computable.
items.exampleCN: 并非每个定义良好的函数都是可计算的。

items.example: Count the boxes before loading them.
items.exampleCN: 装车前先清点箱子。

items.meaning: a record of money; to explain
items.example: The account lists every payment.
items.exampleCN: 这份账目列出每一笔付款。

latinEntries.meaning: to prune, clean; to reckon, think

definition_zh: 计算；算出；估算；预计；打算；设计用于；依赖、指望
definition_en: to work out a number or amount by arithmetic, or to judge what is likely to happen from the evidence available
core_image: 手指在一排小石子上来回点，边点边把数目记进格子
scene: 柜台上摊着账单和几枚硬币，店员低头在纸角写下一串加法。The cashier began to calculate the change while the customer waited.
sceneCN: 这里 calculate 指「做算术、算出数目」（第 1 个义项：做算术计算）；句意：收银员在顾客等候时开始算找零。图中可辨识物件：账单、硬币、纸角、笔。

derivatives.zh: 无法计算的；不可估量的

senses.title: To work with numbers by arithmetic
senses.definition: to perform arithmetic, adding, subtracting, multiplying or dividing, in order to reach a number
senses.definitionCN: 做加减乘除等算术，以求出一个数字
senses.example: The children learned to calculate without counting on their fingers.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们学会了不用掰手指做计算。
senses.why: Calculare came from calculus, the pebble moved on a counting board, so the verb began as moving stones.
senses.whyCN: calculare 出自 calculus，即算板上挪动的石子，因此这个动词最初就是挪石头。

senses.title: To work out a value in mathematics or engineering
senses.definition: to derive a specific quantity by applying formulas or measurements to a problem
senses.definitionCN: 把公式或测量套用到问题上，得出一个具体的量
senses.example: Engineers calculate the load that each beam must carry.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师算出每根梁必须承受多大的荷载。
senses.why: The pebble board became the formula, but the verb still names producing a wanted number.
senses.whyCN: 算板变成了公式，但动词仍然指「把想要的数算出来」。

senses.title: To judge what is likely
senses.definition: to estimate or predict a future amount from the evidence at hand, without needing exact figures
senses.definitionCN: 根据手头证据估算或预测未来的数量，不必有确切数字
senses.example: Analysts calculate that demand will double by spring.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士估计，到春天需求会翻一番。
senses.why: Reckoning with pebbles already implied judging ahead, long before the verb meant forecast.
senses.whyCN: 用石子清点本来就含有预判，远在这个动词表示预报之前。

senses.title: Designed to produce an effect
senses.titleCN: 设计用来产生某种效果
senses.definition: used of an action or remark deliberately arranged to bring about a particular result
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容某个举动或话语被刻意安排以产生特定效果
senses.example: The pause was calculated to make the audience uneasy.
senses.exampleCN: 那段停顿是故意安排的，好让观众不安。
senses.why: The passive turns the reckoning into a plan: the effect was counted on in advance.
senses.whyCN: 被动形式把清点变成计划：效果在事前就被算进去了。

senses.title: To work out cost and profit
senses.definition: to work out the money a venture will spend and earn before deciding whether to go ahead
senses.definitionCN: 先算出某项事业将花多少、赚多少，再决定是否进行
senses.example: The firm calculates its margin before it signs any contract.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在签任何合同之前都会先算出利润率。
senses.why: Commerce made the verb a tool of the counting house, where every stone stood for money.
senses.whyCN: 商业把这个动词变成账房的工具，那里每颗石子都代表钱。

senses.title: To plot a course
senses.definition: to work out a direction or position from charts, stars or instruments, as a ship or an aircraft does
senses.definitionCN: 像船或飞机那样，依据海图、星象或仪器算出方向或位置
senses.example: The navigator calculated a course that kept the ship clear of the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 领航员算出一条让船避开礁石的航线。
senses.why: Navigation is the oldest practical home of the verb after trade, since a course is a number before it is a path.
senses.whyCN: 除商业之外，航海是这个动词最古老的实用领域，因为航线先是一个数，然后才是一条路。

senses.title: To weigh probability and risk
senses.definition: to work out how likely an event is and what it would cost, usually from past records
senses.definitionCN: 通常依据过往记录，算出某事件发生的可能性及其代价
senses.example: Insurers calculate flood risk from decades of rainfall records.
senses.exampleCN: 保险公司根据几十年的降雨记录计算洪水风险。
senses.why: Modern risk work keeps the old counting board, only the stones are now frequencies.
senses.whyCN: 现代的风险工作仍然用那张老算板，只是石子换成了频数。

senses.title: To rely on something
senses.definition: a formal phrasal use meaning to count on or depend on a person, event or condition
senses.definitionCN: 正式的短语用法，意为依靠或指望某人、某事或某条件
senses.example: We calculate upon fair weather for the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 我们指望渡海时天气晴好。
senses.why: To reckon upon a thing is to have already put it into the sum, which is why the phrase means rely.
senses.whyCN: 把某物算进去，就是已经把它放进总数里，因此这个短语意为依赖。

intro.en: Calculate comes from Latin calculare 'to reckon with pebbles', from calculus 'a small stone used on a counting board', a diminutive of calx 'limestone'. English took the verb partly through French in the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: calculate 出自拉丁 calculare「用石子计算」，而 calculus 指「算板上用的计数小石子」，是 calx「石灰岩」的指小形式。英语十五世纪部分经法语引入这个动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Calx meant 'limestone, chalk'; calcium and chalk both trace back to this noun.
items.cn: calx 意为「石灰岩、白垩」；calcium 与 chalk 都可上溯到这个名词。

items.en: Calculus was the diminutive, 'little stone', and specifically the pebble moved on a counting board; English later used it for a stone in the body and for a branch of mathematics.
items.cn: calculus 是指小形式「小石头」，特指算板上挪动的石子；英语后来用它指体内结石，也指一个数学分支。

items.en: Calculare meant 'to move pebbles, to reckon'; the verb named the work done on the board, with no formula in sight.
items.cn: calculare 意为「挪石子、清点」；这个动词命名的是算板上的劳作，当时还看不见公式。

items.en: Medieval schools taught calculare as the art of the abacus, and the verb travelled with the counting board into commerce and navigation.
items.cn: 中世纪的学校把 calculare 当作算盘之术来教，这个动词随算板进入商业与航海。

items.en: English adopted the verb for reckoning, and later broadened it to judging what is likely and planning an effect.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词表示清点，后来又扩展到判断可能之事与安排某种效果。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin calculare, built on the attested noun calculus, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact year of its first English use is not recorded. The deeper origin of calx is not established, and no reconstructed root is asserted.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 calculare，由名词 calculus 构成，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的具体年份没有记录。calx 的更早来源无定论，此处不给出重构词根。

note.en: Group one keeps the Latin pebble and its descendants, where a stone becomes a subject and an adjective; group two holds the other verbs for reaching a number, each with its own temper.
note.cn: 第一组守着拉丁语的那颗石子及其后裔，从石头长成学科名称与形容词；第二组是其他表示「得出数目」的动词，各有各的脾气。

entries.definition: A branch of advanced mathematics, and also a hard mass formed in the body; both grew from the Latin word for a pebble.
entries.definitionCN: 高等数学的一个分支，也指体内形成的硬块；两者都出自拉丁语「石子」一词。

entries.definition: A machine or a person that calculates; the ending -or marks the doer rather than the act.
entries.definitionCN: 做计算的机器或人；词尾 -or 标记施动者，而不是动作。

entries.definition: The act or the result of calculating; it names the process, while calculate names the doing of it.
entries.definitionCN: 计算的动作或结果；它指过程，而 calculate 指做这件事。

entries.definition: Too great or too uncertain to be worked out; the negative prefix denies the ability to calculate.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或不确定到算不出来；否定前缀否定了计算的可能。

entries.definition: To work out a result; it appears more in technical writing and of machines than in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 算出结果；多见于技术写作与机器语境，日常口语较少用。

entries.definition: To work out an amount in the head, or to judge; it carries an older, homelier tone than calculate.
entries.definitionCN: 在心里算出数目，或作判断；比 calculate 更老派、更家常。

entries.definition: To give a rough value without full data; calculate implies a definite procedure, estimate a considered guess.
entries.definitionCN: 在数据不全时给出粗略值；calculate 含明确程序，estimate 含斟酌过的猜测。

entries.definition: To establish a value or a fact with authority; it stresses the settled answer rather than the working.
entries.definitionCN: 权威地确定一个值或事实；强调答案已定，而不是推算过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the counting stone, the plotted course and the phrases that carry the verb into money, risk and formal reliance.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：那颗计数石子、画出的航线，以及把这个动词带进金钱、风险与正式依赖的搭配。

normal.en: Calculus 'little stone' plus -are: move the counting stones.
normal.cn: calculus「小石头」加 -are：挪动计数石子。

normal.en: The same family gives calculator, calculation and incalculable.
normal.cn: 同族词给出 calculator、calculation 与 incalculable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: calculate the cost, calculate the risk, be calculated to.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：计算成本、计算风险、意在。

normal.en: A course is calculated before it is sailed.
normal.cn: 航线先算出来，然后才开船。

normal.en: The formal calculate upon means rely on.
normal.cn: 正式的短语用法意为依赖、指望。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing worn pebbles across a lined board.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把磨圆的小石子推过划了线的板子。

abstract.en: Picture a navigator measuring angles before drawing a route.
abstract.cn: 想象领航员先量角度，再画出航线。

abstract.en: Picture a pause placed on purpose so that a joke lands.
abstract.cn: 想象一段故意留出的停顿，好让笑话生效。

examples.en: The tool can calculate the area of any irregular plot from its outline.
examples.cn: 这个工具能根据轮廓算出任意不规则地块的面积。

examples.en: We calculated that the repair would cost more than a new machine.
examples.cn: 我们算过，修这台机器比买新的还贵。

examples.en: Every remark in the letter was calculated to end the negotiation.
examples.cn: 信里的每句话都是刻意安排的，为的是结束谈判。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cal（石子）+ culate」——拨动算板上的小石子：计算、算出

root: 拉丁 calculare「用石子计算」出自 calculus「计数小石子」，是 calx「石灰岩」的指小形式。同族词有 calculation、calculator、calculus、incalculable。英语十五世纪多经法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the counting stones: plain arithmetic, an engineering value, a forecast, a designed effect, cost and profit, a plotted course, risk and a formal reliance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着这些计数石子：普通算术、工程数值、预测、刻意设计的效果、成本与利润、航线、风险，以及正式的依赖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand moving counting stones on a lined board until a number appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在划线的板上挪动计数石子，直到得出一个数。

branches.en: FROM BOARD TO VALUE: moving stones and applying formulas are one act, only the tool has changed.
branches.cn: 从算板到数值：挪石子与套公式是同一个动作，只是工具换了。

branches.en: JUDGING AHEAD: a forecast and a risk estimate both put a future number into the sum.
branches.cn: 提前判断：预测与风险评估都把未来的数字放进总数里。

branches.en: THE PLANNED EFFECT: the passive turns reckoned steps into a deliberate design.
branches.cn: 预设的效果：被动形式把算好的步骤变成刻意的设计。

branches.en: MONEY AND COURSE: trade and navigation were the two earliest homes of the counting board.
branches.cn: 金钱与航线：商业与航海是算板最早的两个去处。

branches.en: COUNTED ON: whatever is put into the sum is what one ends up relying on.
branches.cn: 被指望的：凡放进总数里的，就是最后所依赖的。

intro.en: Calculate is a Latin verb whose root is a humble noun for a stone, and the same pieces build the device, the noun of the act and the adjective for what cannot be worked out.
intro.cn: calculate 是一个拉丁动词，词根只是一个表示石头的朴素名词，同样的构件也造出计算器、表示动作的名词，以及「算不出来」的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Calx 'limestone' takes the diminutive -ulus to make calculus 'little stone', -are makes the verb calculare, and English adds -ion, -or and -able; in- negates the last.
latinIntro.cn: calx「石灰岩」加指小后缀 -ulus 构成 calculus「小石头」，再加 -are 构成动词 calculare；英语再加 -ion、-or 与 -able，并用 in- 否定最后一个。

items.example: The stone underfoot gave the counting pebble its name.
items.exampleCN: 脚下的石灰岩给了计数石子一个名字。

items.example: The suffix shrinks a block of limestone into a pebble.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一整块石灰岩缩成一颗石子。

items.meaning: a little stone; a counting pebble
items.example: The pebble was the first calculating machine.
items.exampleCN: 这颗石子就是最早的计算机。

items.example: The verb described the hand before it described the mind.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词先描述手，然后才描述头脑。

items.example: She calculates faster than the machine.
items.exampleCN: 她算得比机器还快。

items.meaning: the act or result of calculating
items.example: One calculation showed the plan would fail.
items.exampleCN: 一次计算就表明这个计划行不通。

items.example: The desk calculator still runs on a small cell.
items.exampleCN: 桌上那台计算器还靠一节小电池工作。

items.example: A calculating look crossed his face.
items.exampleCN: 他脸上掠过一丝精明的神色。

items.example: The loss is calculable from the records.
items.exampleCN: 损失可以从记录中算出来。

items.meaning: not able to be worked out
items.meaningCN: 无法计算的；不可估量的
items.example: The damage to the reef was incalculable.
items.exampleCN: 礁石受损程度无法估量。

definition_zh: 计算机；电脑；从事计算的人（旧义）；大型机、服务器；嵌入式处理器；用于模拟与建模的机器；作为一类技术的计算机；把心智比作计算机的隐喻
definition_en: an electronic machine that stores and processes data according to instructions, or, historically, a person who performs calculations
core_image: 一台黑色机箱亮着一排小灯，风扇低声转，屏幕上的数字一行行落下来
scene: 深夜的办公室里只剩一台机器还在响，屏幕上一列数字不断被改写。The computer in the corner kept sorting the survey data while everyone else had gone home.
sceneCN: 这里 computer 指「按指令存储并处理数据的电子机器」（第 1 个义项：处理数据的电子设备）；句意：角落里那台计算机在别人都下班后仍在整理调查数据。图中可辨识物件：机箱、显示器、指示灯、键盘、成列的数据。

senses.title: An electronic machine that handles data
senses.definition: a programmable electronic device that stores information and carries out instructions on it
senses.definitionCN: 可编程的电子设备，能存储信息并按指令处理这些信息
senses.example: Every office now keeps at least one computer for its records.
senses.exampleCN: 现在每个办公室都至少留一台计算机存档案。
senses.why: Compute plus the agent suffix -er names the thing that does the reckoning, once the reckoning moved into electronics.
senses.whyCN: compute 加施事后缀 -er，指做计算的那个东西；计算搬进电子设备后，这个词就落到机器身上。

senses.title: The machine on one person's desk
senses.titleCN: 一个人桌上的那台机器
senses.definition: a general-purpose machine with a screen and keyboard, used by one person at home or at work
senses.definitionCN: 带屏幕和键盘的通用机器，供一个人在家里或工作时使用
senses.example: She moved the photos onto her new computer before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前她把照片转存到了新电脑里。
senses.why: When the machine became small and cheap enough to belong to one person, the general word simply moved onto the desk.
senses.whyCN: 当机器变得又小又便宜、可以归一个人所有，这个通称就自然挪到了办公桌上。

senses.title: A person hired to do long calculations
senses.definition: a person, often a woman, employed to carry out long calculations by hand for astronomy, surveying or artillery tables
senses.definitionCN: 受雇用手工完成长串计算的人，多为女性，为天文、测量或火炮表服务
senses.example: In the wartime office a human computer checked every trajectory table by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 战时办公室里，一位做计算的人逐张手工核对弹道表。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the suffix -er pointed at a worker, and the work was arithmetic, not machinery.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：-er 当时指向一个干活的人，而这份活是算术，不是机器。

senses.title: The large central machine others depend on
senses.titleCN: 别人都依赖的大型中心机器
senses.definition: a large machine that many users or smaller devices rely on for processing, storage or network services
senses.definitionCN: 许多用户或较小的设备依赖它来运算、存储或提供网络服务的大型机器
senses.example: The lab's computer filled a whole room and fed thirty terminals.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室那台计算机占满了一间屋，供三十台终端使用。
senses.why: Big machines kept the plain name while smaller ones took modifiers, so the central machine is still just the computer of the building.
senses.whyCN: 大机器保留了不加修饰的通称，小机器才另加限定词，于是机房里的中心机器仍被叫作这台计算机。

senses.title: The processor hidden inside a device
senses.titleCN: 藏在设备内部的处理器
senses.definition: a small processor built into a car, camera, appliance or instrument, running it without any visible screen
senses.definitionCN: 装在汽车、相机、家电或仪器内部的小型处理器，不通过可见屏幕也能运转该设备
senses.example: The braking system hides a computer that adjusts pressure many times a second.
senses.exampleCN: 刹车系统里藏着一台计算机，每秒多次调整压力。
senses.why: Once a chip could compute, anything that ran itself was said to have a computer inside, even with no keyboard at all.
senses.whyCN: 芯片能算之后，任何自行运转的东西都被说成里面有一台计算机，哪怕根本没有键盘。

senses.title: A machine that imitates a real system
senses.definition: a machine used to imitate a real system, such as weather, traffic or a crash, so that its behaviour can be studied
senses.definitionCN: 用来模仿天气、交通或碰撞等真实系统的机器，以便研究其行为
senses.example: A weather computer ran the storm forward six hours to test the warning.
senses.exampleCN: 一台气象计算机把风暴向前推演六小时，用来检验警报。
senses.why: A simulation is calculation over a model, so the machine that carries it out is named by what it does rather than by its size.
senses.whyCN: 模拟就是对模型做计算，执行它的机器便按功能得名，而不按体积得名。

senses.title: The technology as a force in society
senses.titleCN: 作为社会力量的这门技术
senses.definition: the technology as a whole, treated as something that reshapes work, schooling and daily habits
senses.definitionCN: 把计算机技术整体看作重塑工作、教育与日常习惯的力量
senses.example: The computer changed how offices store and share documents.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机改变了办公室存储与共享文件的方式。
senses.why: Speakers often drop the plural and speak of the machine as a historical agent, which turns a countable device into a mass noun.
senses.whyCN: 说话人常不用复数，而把这台机器当成历史行动者，可数设备于是变成不可数的整体。

senses.title: The mind treated as a machine
senses.definition: the metaphor in which the mind or brain is described as a machine that processes information
senses.definitionCN: 把心灵或大脑描述成处理信息的机器的隐喻
senses.example: The old debate asked whether a brain is really a computer.
senses.exampleCN: 那场旧争论追问大脑是否真是一台计算机。
senses.why: If thought is calculation, then the thing that thinks can be called by the name of the thing that calculates.
senses.whyCN: 如果思维就是计算，那么思考者也可以借用计算者的名字。

intro.en: Computer joins the verb compute, from Latin computare 'to reckon together', with the agent suffix -er. For two centuries the word meant a person who calculates. The machine sense appears in the late nineteenth century and the electronic sense in the 1940s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: computer 由动词 compute 加施事后缀 -er 构成，compute 出自拉丁 computare「一起核算」。此后两个世纪，这个词都指做计算的人。机器义出现在十九世纪末，电子计算机义出现在二十世纪四十年代。年代均为约数。

items.en: Putare meant 'to reckon, count, think', and it also yields repute, dispute and impute; reckoning and thinking share one root.
items.cn: putare 意为「核算、计数、思考」，也衍生出 repute、dispute 与 impute；核算与思考共用同一个词根。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus putare produced computare, 'to reckon together, sum up', the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 putare 构成 computare「合起来核算、求和」，是英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: Computus was the noun for a reckoning, and it survived in medieval Latin for the calculation of church dates.
items.cn: computus 是表示「核算」的名词，在中世纪拉丁语里用于推算教会节期。

items.en: Old French compter 'to count, reckon' carried the word into English, where compute appeared in the seventeenth century as a bookish verb.
items.cn: 古法语 compter「计数、核算」把这个词带进英语，compute 在十七世纪作为书面动词出现。

items.en: The -er form named a person, not a device: a computer was someone employed to work through long calculations.
items.cn: -er 形式当时指人而不指装置：a computer 就是受雇做完长串计算的人。

items.en: Mechanical calculators were already called computers in the late nineteenth century, and electronic machines took the name in the 1940s; first citation uncertain: the exact earliest citation for a machine is not settled.
items.cn: 十九世纪末机械计算器已被叫作计算机，二十世纪四十年代电子机器沿用此名；首见年代不确定：机器义最早书证的具体年份尚无定论。

note.en: Group one is the compute family, where each member names a different grammatical role of the same act; group two holds the everyday rivals for a machine that calculates.
note.cn: 第一组是 compute 词族，每个成员指同一动作的不同语法角色；第二组是日常语言里与「会计算的机器」竞争的词。

entries.definition: To work out an answer by calculation; the verb underneath the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 通过计算得出结果；是名词底下的那个动词。

entries.definition: The act or field of using calculating machines, with no countable device attached.
entries.definitionCN: 使用计算设备的行为或领域，不指某一台可数的装置。

entries.definition: Describing a method or approach that belongs to calculation, rather than naming the machine.
entries.definitionCN: 形容属于计算的方法或路径，而不是给机器命名。

entries.definition: Said of a problem or number that a procedure can in principle work out.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个问题或数值原则上可由某个程序算出。

entries.definition: A small device for arithmetic; it does not store files or run general programs.
entries.definitionCN: 做算术的小装置；不存文件，也不运行通用程序。

entries.definition: A machine defined by answering requests from other machines, whatever its size.
entries.definitionCN: 以回应其他机器请求来定义的机器，与体积无关。

entries.definition: A large central machine of the older style, close to the server sense but tied to a room-sized design.
entries.definitionCN: 旧式的大型中心机器，接近服务器义，但绑定机房规模的设计。

entries.definition: A powerful single-user machine for technical work, between a personal computer and a server.
entries.definitionCN: 供技术工作使用的强力单用户机器，介于个人电脑与服务器之间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the agent suffix, the person who calculates, and the machine that took over the same job.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：施事后缀、做计算的那个人，以及接手同一份活的机器。

normal.en: Compute plus -er: the one who computes.
normal.cn: compute 加 -er：做计算的那一位。

normal.en: Before machines, a computer was a job title for a person.
normal.cn: 在没有机器之前，computer 是一个人的职位名称。

normal.en: The same suffix gives teacher, writer and worker.
normal.cn: 同一个后缀还造出 teacher、writer 与 worker。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: personal computer, computer program, computer network.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：个人电脑、计算机程序、计算机网络。

normal.en: A hidden processor in a car is still called its computer.
normal.cn: 汽车里藏着的处理器仍被叫作它的计算机。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk with columns of figures, then picture a cabinet doing the same columns in a second.
abstract.cn: 先想象一个面对成列数字的职员，再想象一个机柜用一秒钟做完同样的列。

abstract.en: Picture a room-sized machine shrinking until it fits under a wrist.
abstract.cn: 想象一台占满房间的机器不断缩小，最后能戴在手腕上。

abstract.en: Picture a brain drawn as a circuit board, wires where nerves used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象把大脑画成一块电路板，神经的位置换成了导线。

examples.en: The first computers in the observatory were people, not machines.
examples.cn: 天文台最早的 computer 是人，不是机器。

examples.en: A single computer can now hold the archive that once filled a building.
examples.cn: 如今一台计算机就能装下曾经占满一栋楼的档案。

examples.en: Engineers debate whether the brain is a computer or only behaves like one.
examples.cn: 工程师们争论大脑究竟是一台计算机，还是只是表现得像一台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「com（一起）+ put（放）+ er（者）」——把数字放在一起算的那台机器：计算机

root: 拉丁 computare「一起核算」= com-「一起」+ putare「核算、思考」，加施事后缀 -er。同根词有 compute、computation、computable、repute、dispute。十七世纪指人，机器义在十九世纪末出现，电子计算机义在二十世纪四十年代定型。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one agent that reckons: the electronic machine, the machine on a desk, the person paid to calculate, the central machine, the hidden chip, the simulating machine, the technology as a social force and the mind imagined as a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个「做核算者」：电子机器、桌上的那台、受雇做计算的人、中心机器、藏起来的芯片、做模拟的机器、作为社会力量的技术，以及被想象成机器的心灵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that performs calculation, first a person, later a machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个执行计算的主体，先是人，后来是机器。

branches.en: THE DEVICE ITSELF: the general electronic machine and the personal one are the same sense at different scales of ownership.
branches.cn: 装置本身：通用电子机器与个人电脑，是同一义项在归属尺度上的两种样子。

branches.en: THE HUMAN ANCESTOR: before electronics, the -er pointed at a hired calculator, and that sense survives in histories of science.
branches.cn: 人类祖先：电子设备之前，-er 指向受雇的计算者，这个义项仍活在科学史里。

branches.en: BIG AND TINY: the room-sized central machine and the chip hidden in an appliance are opposite ends of the same function.
branches.cn: 大与小：占满房间的中心机器与家电里藏着的芯片，是同一功能的两个极端。

branches.en: THE MACHINE THAT IMITATES: simulation is calculation run over a model, so the tool is named by its task.
branches.cn: 会模仿的机器：模拟是对模型做计算，工具按任务得名。

branches.en: FROM OBJECT TO IDEA: the technology becomes a social force, and then a metaphor for the mind itself.
branches.cn: 从物件到观念：技术先成为社会力量，再成为心灵的隐喻。

intro.en: Computer is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and an English agent suffix; each piece also builds other common words.
intro.cn: computer 由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个英语施事后缀构成，每一部分也都参与构成别的常用词。

latinIntro.en: Com- 'together' joins putare 'to reckon'; the derived computare supplies compute, computation and computer, while -er marks the doer.
latinIntro.cn: com-「一起」与 putare「核算」组合；派生出的 computare 提供 compute、computation 与 computer，-er 则标记执行者。

items.example: The prefix gathers separate numbers into one sum.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把分开的数聚成一个总和。

items.example: Reckoning and thinking grow from the same verb.
items.exampleCN: 核算与思考都从这个动词长出来。

items.meaning: to reckon together; to sum up
items.example: Every English member of the family descends from this verb.
items.exampleCN: 这一族的英语成员都出自这个动词。

items.example: Medieval tables of church dates were a computus.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪推算教会节期的表就是一种核算。

items.example: The suffix first marked a person and later a machine.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀先标记人，后来才标记机器。

items.example: The program can compute the total in a moment.
items.exampleCN: 程序一瞬就能算出总数。

items.meaning: the act or result of calculating
items.example: The computation took longer than the writing.
items.exampleCN: 计算花的时间比写作还长。

items.example: Some problems are not computable in finite time.
items.exampleCN: 有些问题无法在有限时间内算出。

items.example: The archive was computerized last year.
items.exampleCN: 档案馆去年完成了计算机化。

items.meaning: the activity of calculating or using machines
items.meaningCN: 计算或使用机器的活动
items.example: Computing moved from rooms to pockets.
items.exampleCN: 计算从机房走进了口袋。

definition_zh: 计算；使用计算机的活动；计算机科学；机器执行的处理；算力与计算资源；云计算与分布式计算；历史上的算术计算；计算产业
definition_en: the activity or field of using computers and calculating with them, or the processing that machines carry out on data
core_image: 一行指令变成一串数字，再变成屏幕上的一张图
scene: 机房里一整排机柜整夜亮着灯，空调把热风从地板下送上来。Modern computing depends on racks that stay cool all night.
sceneCN: 这里 computing 指「使用计算机的工作与社会性的计算实践」（第 1 个义项：使用计算机进行工作的活动）；句意：现代计算依赖整夜保持低温的机柜。图中可辨识物件：机柜、指示灯、空调出风口、成束的线缆、监控屏幕。

pos.zh: 计算；计算机使用；计算机科学

forms.label: 动词第三人称单数（属 compute）
动词过去式与过去分词（属 compute）

senses.title: The activity of working with computers
senses.titleCN: 使用计算机干活这件事
senses.definition: the activity of working with computers to store, analyse or present information
senses.definitionCN: 使用计算机存储、分析或呈现信息的活动
senses.example: Daily computing in the newsroom means editing copy and checking feeds.
senses.exampleCN: 新闻编辑室每天的计算机工作就是改稿和查信息流。
senses.why: The verbal noun -ing names an activity rather than a device, so the word covers the whole of what people do with machines.
senses.whyCN: 动名词 -ing 命名一种活动而非一台设备，因此这个词覆盖人们用机器做的一整套事情。

senses.title: The academic discipline
senses.definition: the academic field that studies algorithms, software, systems and the theory behind them
senses.definitionCN: 研究算法、软件、系统及其背后理论的学科领域
senses.example: She chose computing as her major because she liked logic more than code.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了计算专业，因为她更喜欢逻辑而不是写代码。
senses.why: A department needs a name for the field, and the activity word is broad enough to hold theory, engineering and applications together.
senses.whyCN: 院系总得给学科一个名字，而表示活动的词足够宽，能把理论、工程与应用都装进去。

senses.title: The processing a machine performs
senses.definition: the operations a machine carries out on data, considered as a process rather than a product
senses.definitionCN: 机器对数据执行的一系列操作，看重过程而非产物
senses.example: The chip does all the computing locally instead of sending it to a distant server.
senses.exampleCN: 芯片在本地完成全部计算，而不是把计算送到远处的服务器。
senses.why: When attention shifts from the machine to what happens inside it, the -ing noun names the processing itself.
senses.whyCN: 当注意力从机器转到机器内部发生的事，-ing 名词就用来指处理本身。

senses.title: Power and resources for calculation
senses.titleCN: 用于计算的算力与资源
senses.definition: the processing power, storage and time that an institution has to buy or allocate
senses.definitionCN: 机构需要采购或分配的算力、存储与机时
senses.example: The budget for computing doubled once the models grew.
senses.exampleCN: 模型变大之后，计算资源的预算翻了一倍。
senses.why: In laboratories and companies the activity becomes a line in a budget, so the mass noun comes to mean the capacity itself.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室与公司里，这项活动会变成预算里的一行，于是不可数名词转而指这份能力。

senses.title: Calculation spread across many machines
senses.titleCN: 分散在许多机器上的计算
senses.definition: the model in which processing and storage are supplied over a network by remote or pooled machines
senses.definitionCN: 通过网络由远程或池化的机器提供处理与存储的模式
senses.example: Cloud computing moved the whole archive off the office machines.
senses.exampleCN: 云计算把整个档案库从办公室的机器上搬走了。
senses.why: Once computing can be rented from a distance, the -ing word attaches to the delivery model rather than to any one device.
senses.whyCN: 当计算可以从远处租用，这个 -ing 词就挂到交付模式上，而不属于任何一台具体设备。

senses.title: Reckoning by hand, the older sense
senses.definition: the older sense of calculation itself, especially arithmetic done with counters, tables or written figures
senses.definitionCN: 指计算本身的旧义，尤指用算筹、表格或纸面数字做的算术
senses.example: Medieval computing meant long division done with counters on a board.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的「计算」指的是在板上用算筹做长除法。
senses.why: Before machines existed, the -ing form simply named the human work of reckoning, and that sense survives in historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 机器出现之前，-ing 形式只表示人做核算这件事，这个义项仍留在历史叙述里。

senses.title: Calculation built into everyday objects
senses.titleCN: 装进日常物件里的计算
senses.definition: the processing embedded in lifts, cars, appliances and sensors, running without a visible screen
senses.definitionCN: 嵌在电梯、汽车、家电与传感器里的处理，不需要可见屏幕也在运行
senses.example: Embedded computing now runs lifts, kettles and door locks.
senses.exampleCN: 嵌入式计算如今在管理电梯、水壶和门锁。
senses.why: When processing disappears into ordinary objects, the activity word is the natural label for something nobody sees.
senses.whyCN: 当处理隐入寻常物件，表示活动的词就成了这种看不见之物的自然标签。

senses.title: The industry that sells calculation
senses.definition: the sector of companies and jobs that build, run or sell computer systems and services
senses.definitionCN: 建造、运营或出售计算机系统与服务的公司与岗位所构成的部门
senses.example: Employment in computing grew faster than in manufacturing.
senses.exampleCN: 计算行业的就业增长快于制造业。
senses.why: An activity sustained by firms turns into an industry, and English happily uses the -ing noun for the sector as well.
senses.whyCN: 由公司维持的活动会变成一个行业，英语也乐于用这个 -ing 名词指整个部门。

intro.en: Computing is the English verbal noun of compute, formed with -ing; compute itself comes from Latin computare 'to reckon together'. The word named arithmetic long before it named the use of electronic machines, and only in the mid-twentieth century did it become the name of a field. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: computing 是 compute 的英语动名词，由 -ing 构成；compute 出自拉丁 computare「一起核算」。这个词先指算术，很久以后才指使用电子机器，直到二十世纪中叶才成为学科名称。年代均为约数。

items.en: Putare 'to reckon, think' is the root verb; repute, dispute and impute belong to the same family.
items.cn: putare「核算、思考」是根动词；repute、dispute 与 impute 属于同一族。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus putare gave computare, 'to reckon together', the source of the English verb compute.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 putare 构成 computare「合起来核算」，是英语动词 compute 的来源。

items.en: Compute entered English in the seventeenth century as a learned verb for reckoning, often in astronomy and navigation.
items.cn: compute 在十七世纪作为书面动词进入英语，表示核算，常用于天文与航海。

items.en: English turns verbs into activity nouns with -ing, so computing first meant the act of reckoning, with no machine in sight.
items.cn: 英语用 -ing 把动词变成活动名词，于是 computing 最初只表示核算这个动作，与机器无关。

items.en: In the 1940s and 1950s the activity moved onto electronic machines, and computing began to mean work done with them.
items.cn: 二十世纪四五十年代，这项活动转移到电子机器上，computing 开始表示用机器完成的工作。

items.en: University departments adopted computing as a field name after the war, and the late twentieth century added cloud computing and distributed computing; first citation uncertain: the precise first academic use of the field name is not settled.
items.cn: 战后大学院系采用 computing 作为学科名，二十世纪末又添上云计算与分布式计算；首见年代不确定：这一学科名最早的学术书证尚无定论。

note.en: Group one is the compute family, where -ing marks the activity while the other forms mark the device, the adjective or the possibility; group two holds words for calculation and for the organised use of data.
note.cn: 第一组是 compute 词族，-ing 标记活动，其余形式分别标记设备、形容词或可能性；第二组是表示计算以及有组织地使用数据的词。

entries.definition: To work out a result by calculation; the activity noun is simply its -ing form.
entries.definitionCN: 通过计算得出结果；活动名词就是它的 -ing 形式。

entries.definition: The countable machine; it answers 'what do you use', not 'what are you doing'.
entries.definitionCN: 可数的机器；回答「你用什么」，而不是「你在做什么」。

entries.definition: Describing methods or costs that belong to calculation, never naming the activity as a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 形容属于计算的方法或代价，从不用作活动的主语。

entries.definition: Said of a task a procedure can in principle finish, a property rather than an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指程序原则上能完成的任务，是一种属性而非活动。

entries.definition: The process of getting a number by arithmetic; it keeps the arithmetic focus without the machines.
entries.definitionCN: 用算术得出一个数的过程；保留算术焦点，不涉及机器。

entries.definition: The branch of mathematics dealing with numbers and basic operations, close to the old sense of computing.
entries.definitionCN: 处理数字与基本运算的数学分支，接近 computing 的旧义。

entries.definition: The study of information systems and their use, often a European name for applied computing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究信息系统及其使用，常是欧洲对应用计算的称呼。

entries.definition: The replacement of human work by machines, which computing makes possible but does not itself name.
entries.definitionCN: 用机器取代人力的过程，computing 使之成为可能，但并不直接指它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the -ing activity noun, the shift from hand arithmetic to machines, and the field that grew out of it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：-ing 活动名词、从手工算术到机器的转移，以及由此长出的学科。

normal.en: Compute plus -ing: the doing, not the thing.
normal.cn: compute 加 -ing：是「做」，不是「物」。

normal.en: The word is uncountable, so it never takes a plural.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数，因此没有复数。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: cloud computing, distributed computing, computing power.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：云计算、分布式计算、算力。

normal.en: Schools and departments use it as the name of a field.
normal.cn: 学校和院系用它作为学科名称。

normal.en: Before machines, it meant arithmetic done by hand.
normal.cn: 在机器之前，它指手工做的算术。

abstract.en: Picture a hand moving counters on a board, then the same movement repeating inside a chip.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在板上移动算筹，然后同样的动作在芯片里反复发生。

abstract.en: Picture work that used to fill a room now arriving over a cable from somewhere else.
abstract.cn: 想象曾经占满一间屋的工作，如今顺着一条线缆从别处送过来。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle, a lift and a lock each quietly doing sums of their own.
abstract.cn: 想象水壶、电梯和门锁各自安静地做着自己的算术。

examples.en: Computing has changed what a small team can finish in one week.
examples.cn: 计算改变了小团队一周能完成的事情。

examples.en: The department teaches computing alongside mathematics and design.
examples.cn: 这个院系把计算与数学、设计一起教。

examples.en: Cheap computing made the old simulation routine available to students.
examples.cn: 廉价的算力让学生也能跑起过去那套模拟流程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「com（一起）+ put（放）+ ing（进行）」——把数字放在一起算的这个过程：计算

root: compute 的英语动名词，-ing 构成活动名词；compute 出自拉丁 computare「一起核算」= com-「一起」+ putare「核算」。同根词有 computer、computation、computational。先指手工算术，二十世纪中叶起指使用电子机器的活动与学科。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one activity: daily work with machines, the academic field, the processing inside a machine, the power bought for it, calculation spread over a network, hand reckoning, processing hidden in objects and the industry that sells it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一项活动：日常用机器干活、学科本身、机器内部的处理、为它采购的算力、散布在网络上的计算、手工核算、藏进物件里的处理，以及出售它的行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the act of reckoning, carried out first by hand and later by machines.
core.cn: 核心意象：核算这个动作，先由人手工完成，后来交由机器完成。

branches.en: THE SAME ACT, TWO ERAS: working at a screen today and moving counters on a board long ago are one activity with different tools.
branches.cn: 同一动作，两个时代：今天在屏幕前工作，与很久以前在板上移算筹，是同一项活动换了工具。

branches.en: FROM ACTIVITY TO INSTITUTION: what people do becomes a department, and departments become an industry.
branches.cn: 从活动到建制：人们做的事变成一个院系，院系又变成一个行业。

branches.en: THE INSIDE VIEW: the word can name the operations themselves, not only the work around them.
branches.cn: 内部视角：这个词也能指那些操作本身，而不只是围绕它们的劳动。

branches.en: METERED AND DISTRIBUTED: capacity becomes something bought, and then something delivered from elsewhere.
branches.cn: 可计量且可分发：算力先变成可采购之物，再变成从别处送来的服务。

branches.en: INVISIBLE EVERYWHERE: processing disappears into lifts and locks, where no screen marks it.
branches.cn: 无处不在却看不见：处理隐入电梯与门锁，那里没有屏幕标记它。

intro.en: Computing is a Latin root wrapped in an English verb ending and then turned into an activity noun; each layer also builds other words.
intro.cn: computing 是一个拉丁词根套上英语动词词尾、再转为活动名词的结果，每一层也都参与构造别的词。

latinIntro.en: Com- 'together' plus putare 'to reckon' make computare, which gives compute, computation and computer; English -ing then makes the activity noun from the verb.
latinIntro.cn: com-「一起」与 putare「核算」构成 computare，进而给出 compute、computation 与 computer；英语的 -ing 再从动词造出活动名词。

items.example: The prefix joins separate figures into one reckoning.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把分开的数字并进同一次核算。

items.example: The root covers counting and judging at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时涵盖计数与判断。

items.example: The Latin verb is the ancestor of every English form here.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是这里所有英语形式的祖先。

items.meaning: the act or process of doing
items.example: The suffix turns a verb into the name of an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成活动的名称。

items.example: The machine can compute the sum instantly.
items.exampleCN: 机器能立刻算出这个和。

items.example: The computation filled the whole afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 这次计算占满了整个下午。

items.example: Computing is uncountable in this sense.
items.exampleCN: 在这个义项里它是不可数名词。

items.example: The suffix first meant a person, then a device.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀先指人，后指装置。

items.example: The adjective describes the method rather than the machine.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述方法而非机器。

items.example: The task is computationally cheap.
items.exampleCN: 这项任务在计算上开销很小。

definition_zh: 计算的；与计算有关的；借助计算机完成的；计算代价与复杂度的；计算模型与仿真的；以计算方法命名的学科的；数值误差与计算精度的；认知科学中「心智即计算」的
definition_en: relating to calculation, or describing work that is carried out by methods of calculation and often by machines
core_image: 一张网格纸被切成无数小格，每一格同时被算过一遍
scene: 实验室的墙上贴着一张被切成许多小方格的网格纸，每一格都标着一个步骤。Their computational approach splits the image into small patches and scores each one.
sceneCN: 这里 computational 指「属于计算模型与仿真方法的」（第 4 个义项：以计算模型处理问题）；句意：他们的计算式方法把图像切成小块，再逐块打分。图中可辨识物件：网格纸、小方格、步骤标号、屏幕、放大镜。

derivatives.zh: 在计算方面；从计算角度

senses.title: Belonging to calculation in general
senses.definition: relating to calculation itself, whether done by hand, by formula or by machine
senses.definitionCN: 与计算本身有关，不论计算由手工、公式还是机器完成
senses.example: The paper keeps the computational part separate from the field study.
senses.exampleCN: 论文把计算部分与实地研究分开处理。
senses.why: The suffix -al simply says 'of or belonging to', so the adjective can attach to calculation without naming any device.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 只表示「属于」，因此这个形容词可以挂在计算上，而不提任何装置。

senses.title: Done with a machine rather than by hand
senses.definition: carried out by machine methods instead of manual or purely theoretical work
senses.definitionCN: 以机器方法而非手工或纯理论方式完成的
senses.example: A computational shortcut saved the team weeks of laboratory work.
senses.exampleCN: 一条计算捷径为团队省下了数周的实验室工作。
senses.why: Once most long calculations moved to machines, the adjective became a practical label for the machine route.
senses.whyCN: 当长串计算大多转到机器上，这个形容词就成了机器路线的实用标签。

senses.title: The price of running an algorithm
senses.titleCN: 运行算法要付出的代价
senses.definition: the time, memory or number of steps that an algorithm costs as its input grows
senses.definitionCN: 算法随输入增大而耗费的时间、内存或步骤数
senses.example: The team measured the computational cost before scaling up.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在扩大规模之前先测量了计算成本。
senses.why: If a method is to be judged practical, its demands need a name, and that name is the adjective attached to cost or complexity.
senses.whyCN: 要判断一种方法是否实用，就得给它的开销一个名字，这名字就是挂在成本或复杂度前的这个形容词。

senses.title: Models and simulation
senses.definition: describing a model or simulation that represents a system by rules a machine can run
senses.definitionCN: 形容用机器可执行的规则来表征某个系统的模型或仿真
senses.example: A computational model of the climate ran a century in an afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 一个气候计算模型在一个下午里跑完了一百年。
senses.why: A model becomes computational when its behaviour is produced by step-by-step calculation rather than by physical resemblance.
senses.whyCN: 当一个模型的行为由逐步计算产生、而非靠实物相似，它就是计算模型。

senses.title: A discipline named by its method
senses.definition: used in the names of fields, such as computational linguistics or computational biology, that apply calculation to another subject
senses.definitionCN: 用于学科名称，如计算语言学或计算生物学，表示把计算应用到另一门学问
senses.example: The field of computational linguistics borrows tools from statistics and grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 计算语言学借用了统计与语法的工具。
senses.why: When a field is defined by its method rather than its subject, the adjective moves in front of the subject name and stays there.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学问靠方法而非题材定义，这个形容词就移到题材名前面并固定下来。

senses.title: Thinking in steps a machine could follow
senses.titleCN: 按机器能照做的步骤思考
senses.definition: describing the kind of problem solving that breaks a task into ordered steps, decomposition and abstraction
senses.definitionCN: 形容把任务拆成有序步骤、分解与抽象的问题解决方式
senses.example: Schools now teach computational thinking before any programming language.
senses.exampleCN: 学校现在先教计算思维，再教任何编程语言。
senses.why: The adjective reaches beyond machinery to a habit of mind, because the same ordered steps can be taught without a device.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词越出机器，指向一种思维习惯，因为同一套有序步骤不用设备也能教。

senses.title: Error and precision in numbers
senses.definition: relating to the rounding, truncation and instability that arise when calculation is done with finite precision
senses.definitionCN: 与有限精度计算中出现的舍入、截断与不稳定性有关
senses.example: Each extra step added a computational error to the total.
senses.exampleCN: 每多一步，总数里就多一份计算误差。
senses.why: Machines work with limited digits, so the adjective also marks the flaws that calculation introduces into an answer.
senses.whyCN: 机器只有有限的位数，因此这个形容词也标记计算给答案引入的缺陷。

senses.title: The mind described as calculation
senses.definition: in cognitive science, holding that mental processes are operations on representations, in the manner of a calculation
senses.definitionCN: 在认知科学中主张心理过程是对表征的运算，其方式如同计算
senses.example: Some psychologists defend a computational view of memory.
senses.exampleCN: 一些心理学家为记忆的计算观辩护。
senses.why: If the mind performs operations on symbols, then every mental theory built on that picture can carry the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 如果心灵对符号执行运算，那么建立在这幅图景上的每一种心智理论都能带这个形容词。

intro.en: Computational is computation plus the adjective suffix -al, from Latin -alis. Computation descends from Latin computatio, a noun of action from computare 'to reckon together'. The adjective became common only in the twentieth century, with the growth of numerical methods and machine calculation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: computational 由 computation 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，-al 出自拉丁 -alis。computation 出自拉丁 computatio，是 computare「一起核算」的动作名词。这个形容词到二十世纪才随数值方法与机器计算的兴起而通行。年代均为约数。

items.en: Putare 'to reckon, think' is the root; repute, dispute and impute share it.
items.cn: putare「核算、思考」是词根；repute、dispute 与 impute 共用它。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus putare made computare, 'to reckon together', the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 putare 构成 computare「合起来核算」，是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: Computatio was the action noun 'a reckoning', formed with -io from the same verb.
items.cn: computatio 是动作名词「核算」，由同一动词加 -io 构成。

items.en: -alis was the ordinary Latin suffix for 'belonging to', and it becomes -al in English adjectives such as national and natural.
items.cn: -alis 是拉丁语里表示「属于」的常用后缀，在英语形容词里变成 -al，如 national 与 natural。

items.en: English took computation through French in the Middle Ages, at first for any reckoning or account.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪经法语引入 computation，最初泛指任何核算或账目。

items.en: Computational spread with numerical analysis and machine calculation, then into field names; first citation uncertain: the earliest English use of the adjective is not securely dated.
items.cn: computational 随数值分析与机器计算传播，后来又进入学科名；首见年代不确定：这个形容词最早的英语用例年代没有可靠定论。

note.en: Group one is the compute family: the noun, the device, the verb and the possibility all look alike but play different roles. Group two holds adjectives that describe how a result was obtained.
note.cn: 第一组是 compute 词族：名词、设备、动词与可能性外形相似，却各扮不同角色。第二组是描述结果如何获得的形容词。

entries.definition: A single calculation or its result, countable when it means one run and uncountable as a process.
entries.definitionCN: 一次计算或其结果；指一次运行时可数，指过程时不可数。

entries.definition: The countable machine; the adjective never points at a machine directly.
entries.definitionCN: 可数的机器；这个形容词从不直接指向某台机器。

entries.definition: To carry out a calculation; the adjective is the description built on the noun, not on the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 执行计算；这个形容词是建立在名词而非动词上的描述。

entries.definition: Able to be calculated in principle; it judges a problem, while computational describes a method.
entries.definitionCN: 原则上可被算出；它判断问题，而 computational 描述方法。

entries.definition: Carried out by approximating with numbers, often in contrast to an exact symbolic solution.
entries.definitionCN: 以数值近似来完成，常与精确的符号解相对。

entries.definition: Defined by a step-by-step procedure, whether or not a machine runs it.
entries.definitionCN: 由逐步程序来定义，不论是否由机器执行。

entries.definition: Belonging to mathematics at large, of which calculation is only one part.
entries.definitionCN: 属于整个数学，计算只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: Produced as an imitation of a real system; it describes the output rather than the calculating method.
entries.definitionCN: 作为真实系统的模仿产物；描述输出而非计算方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the -al adjective, the cost and complexity of algorithms, and the field names built on the word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：-al 形容词、算法的时间与复杂度代价，以及用这个词构造的学科名。

normal.en: Computation plus -al: of or belonging to calculation.
normal.cn: computation 加 -al：属于计算的。

normal.en: It describes the method, never the machine itself.
normal.cn: 它描述方法，从不直接描述机器本身。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: computational model, computational cost, computational linguistics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：计算模型、计算成本、计算语言学。

normal.en: The adverb form is computationally, as in computationally cheap.
normal.cn: 副词形式是 computationally，如「计算上开销小」。

normal.en: Limit states are more and most computational, not -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级用 more 与 most，不用 -er 与 -est。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of graph paper cut into a thousand squares, each worked through at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一张方格纸被切成一千格，每一格同时被算一遍。

abstract.en: Picture a stopwatch running beside an algorithm as the input doubles.
abstract.cn: 想象输入翻倍时，一只秒表在算法旁边计时。

abstract.en: Picture a mind drawn as arrows moving between small labelled boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象把心灵画成在许多带标签的小方框之间移动的箭头。

examples.en: The two approaches differ in their computational demands, not in their aims.
examples.cn: 两种路径的差别在计算需求上，而不在目标上。

examples.en: A computational model can fail for reasons that no experiment would reveal.
examples.cn: 计算模型可能因为实验无法揭示的原因而失败。

examples.en: Her argument turns on a computational account of how sentences are parsed.
examples.cn: 她的论证关键在于一套关于句子如何被解析的计算解释。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「comput（算）+ ation（行为）+ al（的）」——属于计算那一套的：计算的、计算式的

root: computation + -al；computation 出自拉丁 computatio「核算」，computatio 又出自 computare「一起核算」= com-「一起」+ putare「核算」。同根词有 compute、computer、computable、computationally。形容词义在二十世纪随数值方法与机器计算通行。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: belonging to calculation, done by machine, the cost of an algorithm, a model that runs, a field named by its method, an ordered habit of thought, the error of finite precision and the mind treated as calculation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个形容词：属于计算、由机器完成、算法的代价、能跑起来的模型、以方法命名的学科、有序的思维习惯、有限精度带来的误差，以及被当成计算的心灵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the quality of being produced by step-by-step calculation rather than by direct observation.
core.cn: 核心意象：由逐步计算产生、而非由直接观察得来的那种性质。

branches.en: FROM BELONGING TO DOING: the general 'of calculation' sense narrows into 'done by machine' once machines take over the work.
branches.cn: 从归属到执行：泛泛的「属于计算」在机器接手后收窄为「由机器完成」。

branches.en: THE PRICE TAG: every method has a cost in time and memory, and the adjective names that cost.
branches.cn: 代价标签：每种方法都有时间与内存上的开销，这个形容词就给这份开销命名。

branches.en: THE MODEL THAT RUNS: a representation becomes computational when rules, not resemblance, produce its behaviour.
branches.cn: 会跑的模型：当行为由规则而非相似性产生，一个表征就成了计算模型。

branches.en: METHOD INTO NAME: the adjective prefixes whole disciplines, and then hardens into a way of thinking taught on its own.
branches.cn: 方法变成名称：这个形容词加到整门学科前面，随后凝固成一种可单独教授的思维方式。

branches.en: FLAW AND THEORY: finite digits leave error in the answer, while the same picture of stepwise operations becomes a theory of mind.
branches.cn: 缺陷与理论：有限的位数给答案留下误差，而同一幅逐步运算的图景又成了心智理论。

intro.en: Computational stacks a Latin root, a Latin action-noun ending and a Latin adjective ending; each layer is productive in English.
intro.cn: computational 叠了一个拉丁词根、一个拉丁动作名词词尾与一个拉丁形容词词尾，每一层在英语里都能产词。

latinIntro.en: Putare 'to reckon' yields computare and then computatio; -alis 'belonging to' gives English -al, which turns the noun into an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: putare「核算」生出 computare，再出 computatio；-alis「属于」给出英语 -al，把名词变成形容词。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把数字聚成一个总和。

items.example: Counting and judging grow from one root.
items.exampleCN: 计数与判断从同一个词根长出。

items.example: The verb supplies the whole English family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词供给整个英语词族。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of computation.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是 computation 的基础。

items.meaning: relating to; of the kind of
items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: The noun is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词的基础。

items.example: The model is computational rather than physical.
items.exampleCN: 这个模型是计算的，而非实物的。

items.example: The method is computationally expensive.
items.exampleCN: 这种方法在计算上很昂贵。

items.example: The term computationality is rare in ordinary use.
items.exampleCN: computationality 在日常使用中很罕见。

items.example: Machines compute far faster than people.

definition_zh: 计算机科学；研究计算与信息的学科；该学科的课程与知识体系；理论计算机科学；应用计算机科学；大学的计算机科学系；学位与职业方向；研究共同体
definition_en: the academic study of computation, information and the systems that process them, together with the courses, departments and research community built around that study

sceneCN: 这里 computer science 指「研究计算与信息的学科」（第 1 个义项：把计算过程与信息本身当作研究对象的学科）；句意：她选择计算机科学，是因为想看到关于算法的证明如何变成一段能运行的程序。图中可辨识物件：阶梯教室、黑板、算法步骤、笔记本电脑。
