senses.title: The study of computation and information
senses.titleCN: 研究计算与信息的学科
senses.definition: the academic discipline that studies what can be computed, how information is represented, and how machines process it
senses.definitionCN: 研究可计算的范围、信息如何表示以及机器如何处理信息的学科
senses.example: Computer science asks which problems a machine can solve and how efficiently it can solve them.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机科学追问哪些问题机器能解，以及能多高效地解。
senses.why: The name pairs the machine with the old word for organised knowledge, so it names a field of study rather than a device.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字把机器与表示系统知识的旧词并置，指一门学问而不是一台设备。

senses.title: The courses that teach the field
senses.titleCN: 讲授这门学科的一系列课程
senses.definition: the set of courses and the body of knowledge taught under this name in schools and universities
senses.definitionCN: 学校与大学里以这个名称开设的课程及其知识体系
senses.example: First-year computer science covers logic, data structures and programming.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机科学一年级课程包括逻辑、数据结构与程序设计。
senses.why: A discipline becomes a timetable, and the same two words then name the subjects a student sits through.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科会变成一张课表，同样两个词于是也指学生要上完的那些科目。

senses.title: The theory of what can be computed
senses.definition: the branch that studies algorithms, complexity and the limits of computation, often called theoretical computer science
senses.definitionCN: 研究算法、复杂度与计算极限的分支，常称理论计算机科学
senses.example: Theoretical computer science shows that some problems have no efficient solution at all.
senses.exampleCN: 理论计算机科学证明有些问题根本不存在高效解法。
senses.why: Theory sits at the centre of the field, so its name is simply the discipline's name with a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 理论位于这门学科的核心，因此它的名称只是学科名加一个限定词。

senses.title: The applied branch that builds systems
senses.definition: the branch that turns theory into working systems, networks and programs, often called applied computer science
senses.definitionCN: 把理论变成可运行的系统、网络与程序的分支，常称应用计算机科学
senses.example: Applied computer science turns a proof about sorting into a library that other programs can call.
senses.exampleCN: 应用计算机科学把关于排序的证明变成别的程序可以调用的库。
senses.why: Once the theory is settled, the same name carries the work of making it run.
senses.whyCN: 理论确定之后，同一个名称也承载把它跑起来的工作。

senses.title: A department in a university
senses.definition: the academic unit that employs the field's teachers and houses its students
senses.definitionCN: 聘用该领域教师、容纳其学生的学术单位
senses.example: The computer science department shares a building with mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机科学系与数学系共用一栋楼。
senses.why: Institutions borrow the discipline's name for the room, the staff and the budget that keep it alive.
senses.whyCN: 机构借用学科名来指维持这门学科的房间、人员与预算。

senses.title: A degree and a career path
senses.definition: the qualification and the jobs that follow from studying the field
senses.definitionCN: 学习这门学科所得的资格以及随之而来的工作岗位
senses.example: A degree in computer science opened research posts and industry jobs alike.
senses.exampleCN: 一个计算机科学学位同时打开了研究岗位与业界职位。
senses.why: What is studied becomes what is certified, and the certificate takes the name of the subject.
senses.whyCN: 所学的东西会变成被认证的资格，证书便沿用学科之名。

senses.title: A research community and its papers
senses.definition: the international community of researchers, conferences, journals and accumulated papers
senses.definitionCN: 由研究者、会议、期刊与积累的论文组成的国际共同体
senses.example: Computer science keeps its own conferences, journals and a shared archive of preprints.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机科学有自己的会议、期刊和共享的预印本档案。
senses.why: A field is also the people who cite each other, and their shared name marks that network.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科也是那些互相引用的人，共同的名称标记着这张网络。

senses.title: How it differs from information technology
senses.definition: the boundary that separates the study of computing principles from the practical management of systems
senses.definitionCN: 把计算原理的研究与系统的实际管理区分开的界线
senses.example: Computer science explains why an algorithm is fast, while information technology keeps the servers running.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机科学解释一种算法为什么快，信息技术则让服务器持续运转。
senses.why: When two names compete for the same jobs, the older one claims the principles and the newer one claims the practice.
senses.whyCN: 当两个名称争夺同一批岗位时，较早的名称主张原理，较新的名称主张实务。

intro.en: Computer science is a twentieth-century compound of two older words. Computer goes back through French to Latin computare 'to reckon, calculate', and science to Latin scientia 'knowledge', a noun from scire 'to know'. The phrase settled into English in the 1950s and 1960s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: computer science 是二十世纪由两个更古老的词组成的短语。computer 经法语上溯到拉丁 computare「计算、清算」，science 上溯到拉丁 scientia「知识」，后者出自 scire「知道」。这个短语在二十世纪五十至六十年代进入英语并稳定下来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Computare meant 'to reckon together, calculate', built from com- 'together' and putare 'to reckon, settle'; it is the direct source of compute and computer.
items.cn: computare 意为「合起来计算、清算」，由 com-「一起」与 putare「计算、结算」构成；它是 compute 与 computer 的直接来源。

items.en: Putare meant 'to reckon, think, prune'; its deeper pre-Latin origin is reconstructed rather than attested, and the usual reconstruction is offered as a form, not as an attested word.
items.cn: putare 意为「计算、思考、修剪」；它在拉丁语之前的更深来源属于重构形式，通常给出的只是重构，并非有据可查的词。

items.en: Scientia was a noun for 'knowledge, understanding', formed from the verb scire with an abstract noun ending; English science descends from it through French.
items.cn: scientia 是表示「知识、理解」的名词，由动词 scire 加抽象名词词尾构成；英语 science 经法语出自它。

items.en: Scire meant 'to know', and it also underlies conscious and conscience, where knowing is shared with oneself.
items.cn: scire 意为「知道」，也是 conscious 与 conscience 的词源，那里「知道」是与自己共享的。

items.en: Computer first named a person who did calculations; the machine sense took over in the mid-twentieth century, and only then could the compound name a field.
items.cn: computer 最初指做计算的人；机器义在二十世纪中期占据主导，此后这个复合词才能用来指一门学科。

items.en: Universities began offering programs under this name in the 1950s and 1960s; first citation uncertain: the exact first printed use is not recorded, so the dating is given as approximate.
items.cn: 大学在二十世纪五十至六十年代开始以这个名称开设课程；首见年代不确定：最早书证的具体出处没有记录，因此年代只作约数。

note.en: Group one follows the words that share the computer and science stock; group two holds neighbouring fields that are often confused with the discipline.
note.cn: 第一组是共用 computer 与 science 词干的词；第二组是常与本学科混淆的邻近领域。

entries.definition: The device or, earlier, the person who calculates; it names an object, while the phrase names a discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 指设备，更早也指做计算的人；它命名一个物件，而这个短语命名一门学科。

entries.definition: The practice or activity of using and building computer systems, closer to a process than to an academic subject.
entries.definitionCN: 使用与构建计算机系统的实践或活动，更接近一个过程，而非一门学科。

entries.definition: A researcher or practitioner of the field; the human counterpart of the discipline's name.
entries.definitionCN: 该领域的研究者或从业者；是学科名称在人的层面的对应说法。

entries.definition: Organised knowledge tested by observation; standing alone it covers physics, chemistry and biology, not computing.
entries.definitionCN: 经观察检验的系统知识；单独使用时涵盖物理、化学与生物，不含计算。

entries.definition: The study of information systems, often applied and European in flavour; it overlaps with the field but stresses data handling.
entries.definitionCN: 研究信息系统的学问，偏应用，欧洲用法较多；与本学科重叠，但强调数据处理。

entries.definition: The management and support of systems in use; it applies what the discipline studies.
entries.definitionCN: 对使用中的系统进行管理与支持；它应用本学科所研究的内容。

entries.definition: The engineering discipline of constructing and maintaining programs; narrower than the whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 构建与维护程序的工程学科；比整门学科窄。

entries.definition: The extraction of knowledge from data using statistics and computing; related but centred on inference from datasets.
entries.definitionCN: 用统计与计算从数据中提取知识；与之相关，但核心是从数据集做推断。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two Latin roots, a department sign and the theory-practice split.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁词根、一块系牌，以及理论与应用的分界。

normal.en: Computer is the tool; science is organised knowledge, so the phrase names what is known about computing.
normal.cn: computer 是工具，science 是系统知识，所以这个短语命名的是关于计算的已知内容。

normal.en: Latin computare 'to reckon' plus scire 'to know': reckon and know.
normal.cn: 拉丁 computare「计算」加 scire「知道」：一边算，一边知。

normal.en: A department, a degree and a journal all wear the same two words.
normal.cn: 一个系、一个学位、一本期刊，挂的都是同样两个词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: computer science department, theoretical computer science, applied computer science.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：计算机科学系、理论计算机科学、应用计算机科学。

normal.en: The short form CS fits on a timetable and a building sign.
normal.cn: 缩写 CS 正好写进课表和楼牌。

abstract.en: Picture a blackboard of steps that a machine can follow line by line.
abstract.cn: 想象一块黑板，上面的步骤能被机器一行行照着执行。

abstract.en: Picture a proof sheet lying beside a running program.
abstract.cn: 想象一张证明纸与一段正在运行的程序并排躺着。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of conference papers growing in the same call-number range.
abstract.cn: 想象一排会议论文在同一个索书号区间里不断增多。

examples.en: Computer science grew out of mathematics and engineering departments after the war.
examples.cn: 战后，计算机科学从数学系与工程系中生长出来。

examples.en: She teaches computer science to students who have never written a program.
examples.cn: 她给从未写过程序的学生教计算机科学。

examples.en: Job adverts often blur the line between computer science and information technology.
examples.cn: 招聘广告常常模糊计算机科学与信息技术之间的界线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「computer（计算机）+ science（科学）」——关于计算与信息的科学：算法、理论、系统与学位

root: computer 出自拉丁 computare「计算、清算」，science 出自拉丁 scientia「知识」，scientia 又出自 scire「知道」；短语在二十世纪五十至六十年代确立。同根词有 compute、computation、scientific、conscious。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one discipline from its object of study to its social forms: the field, its courses, theory, applied work, a department, a degree, a research community and its border with information technology.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一门学科从研究对象走到社会形态：学科本身、课程、理论、应用、一个系、一个学位、一个研究共同体，以及它与信息技术的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a discipline that treats calculation and information as objects of study, not as a machine to be sold.
core.cn: 核心意象：一门把计算与信息当作研究对象的学问，而不是一台待售的机器。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND WHAT IT TEACHES: the discipline itself and the timetable through which it reaches students.
branches.cn: 学科与其所授：学科本身，以及它抵达学生的那张课表。

branches.en: THEORY AND BUILD: one branch proves the limits, the other turns proofs into running systems.
branches.cn: 理论与建造：一支证明极限，一支把证明变成运行的系统。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND CAREER: a department houses the work, a degree carries it into a job.
branches.cn: 机构与职业：系安置工作，学位把它带进岗位。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY: conferences, journals and citations make a field visible as a network of people.
branches.cn: 共同体：会议、期刊与引用让一门学科显形为一张人的网络。

branches.en: THE BORDER: against information technology, principles are claimed by the older name and practice by the newer one.
branches.cn: 边界：面对信息技术，原理归较早的名称，实务归较新的名称。

intro.en: Computer science joins a Latin-derived technical noun to a Latin-derived noun for knowledge, and each part still forms other English words.
intro.cn: computer science 把一个源自拉丁语的技术名词与一个源自拉丁语的知识名词连在一起，两部分至今都参与构成别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Computare 'to reckon' supplies computer, computation and computational; scientia and scire 'to know' supply science, scientific and conscious, while -or and -ia are Latin noun endings.
latinIntro.cn: computare「计算」衍生出 computer、computation 与 computational；scientia 与 scire「知道」衍生出 science、scientific 与 conscious，-or 与 -ia 则是拉丁名词词尾。

items.example: The prefix joins the act of reckoning to something shared.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把计算的动作连成一件共同的事。

items.example: Computare is built on this verb plus a prefix.
items.exampleCN: computare 就是这个词加前缀构成的。

items.example: To compute is to carry out this reckoning.
items.exampleCN: 「计算」这个词就是执行这种计算。

items.meaning: one who reckons; a calculating machine
items.example: The agent ending first named a person, then a machine.
items.exampleCN: 这个施动词尾先指人，后指机器。

items.example: The ending also builds operator and inspector.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾也构成 operator 与 inspector。

items.example: Science reached English through French from this noun.
items.exampleCN: science 经法语从这个名词进入英语。

items.example: Conscious and conscience share this verb.
items.exampleCN: conscious 与 conscience 共用这个动词。

items.example: The ending turns a verb root into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词词根变成表示状态的名词。

items.example: A scientist is a person who practises a science.
items.exampleCN: scientist 就是从事一门科学的人。

items.example: Computational describes work done by calculation.
items.exampleCN: computational 描述靠计算完成的工作。

definition_en: the programs, data and instructions that a computer runs, together with the industry that produces them and, figuratively, the learned rules a mind follows

senses.title: Programs and data taken as a whole
senses.definition: the programs, data and instructions that a computer runs, taken as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 计算机运行所需的程序、数据与指令的总和
senses.example: The new software runs on both desktops and phones.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新软件在台式机与手机上都能运行。
senses.why: Ware means goods, so software is simply the goods that are soft: what a machine carries rather than what it is made of.
senses.whyCN: ware 意为货物，software 就是「软的货物」：机器承载的东西，而不是构成它的材料。

senses.title: One application or product
senses.definition: one program or product that a user installs, opens or buys
senses.definitionCN: 用户安装、打开或购买的某一个程序或产品
senses.example: The accounting software crashed on the last day of the quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 那款会计软件在季度的最后一天崩溃了。
senses.why: Trade talk names a product by the material it is made of, so one title can stand for the whole category.
senses.whyCN: 商业用语用材料名称来指产品，于是一个具体产品的名字可以代表整个类别。

senses.title: System software next to the machine
senses.definition: the layer that runs the machine itself, such as operating systems and drivers
senses.definitionCN: 运行机器本身的那一层，如操作系统与驱动程序
senses.example: System software starts before any application can load.
senses.exampleCN: 系统软件在任何应用加载之前就已启动。
senses.why: The layer closest to the machine is still goods you cannot touch, so the same word covers it with a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 离机器最近的那一层仍是摸不到的货物，于是同一个词加个限定语就能覆盖它。

senses.title: Application software for the user's task
senses.titleCN: 面向用户任务的应用软件
senses.definition: programs written for a user's task rather than for the machine's own operation
senses.definitionCN: 为用户的任务而非机器自身运转编写的程序
senses.example: Application software is what people open to write, draw or calculate.
senses.exampleCN: 应用软件就是人们打开来写字、画图或计算的程序。
senses.why: Once the machine layer is named, the layer above needs only the word for use.
senses.whyCN: 机器那一层有了名字，上面那一层只需再加上表示「应用」的词。

senses.title: The software industry
senses.definition: the business of writing, selling and maintaining programs
senses.definitionCN: 编写、出售与维护程序的行业
senses.example: Software became the region's largest export, ahead of shipping.
senses.exampleCN: 软件成为该地区最大的出口项目，超过航运。
senses.why: An industry is named after what it makes, so the material word turns into a sector.
senses.whyCN: 产业以其制造之物命名，材料词于是变成一个行业。

senses.title: Source code and instructions as written
senses.definition: the code, listings and instructions as written, apart from any machine that runs them
senses.definitionCN: 写下来的代码、清单与指令，与运行它们的机器分开看待
senses.example: He read the software line by line before trusting the build.
senses.exampleCN: 在信任这个构建之前，他逐行读了软件源码。
senses.why: What is written is the most literal kind of soft goods, existing as text before it ever runs.
senses.whyCN: 写下来的东西是最字面的软货物，在运行之前先以文本存在。

senses.title: Software supplied with a device
senses.definition: programs supplied with a device, often before the owner chooses them
senses.definitionCN: 随设备提供的程序，往往在机主选择之前就已装入
senses.example: The laptop shipped with software that the owner never asked for.
senses.exampleCN: 这台笔记本出厂时带了机主从没要求过的软件。
senses.why: Bundling turns goods into a default, and the same word travels with the machine.
senses.whyCN: 捆绑销售把货物变成默认配置，同一个词就随机器一起交付。

senses.title: Learned rules in the mind
senses.definition: figurative use for the habits, rules and routines installed in a person by training or culture
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：训练或文化在一个人身上装好的习惯、规则与常规
senses.example: The rules he grew up with became software for his daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 他从小接受的规矩成了他日常生活的软件。
senses.why: If a brain is treated as a machine, its learned routines become the programs it runs.
senses.whyCN: 若把大脑看作机器，它习得的常规就成了它运行的程序。

intro.en: Software is a native English compound, not a Latin borrowing. Soft descends from Old English sōfte 'gentle, not hard', and ware from Old English waru 'goods, merchandise'. The compound was coined in the mid-twentieth century as the counterpart of hardware. It has no Latin source.
intro.cn: software 是英语本族复合词，不是拉丁语借词。soft 出自古英语 sōfte「柔软、不硬」，ware 出自古英语 waru「货物、商品」。这个复合词在二十世纪中期作为 hardware 的对举而造，没有拉丁来源。

items.en: Sōfte meant 'gentle, mild, not hard'; it survives in soft and in soften, and it describes texture rather than value.
items.cn: sōfte 意为「温和的、不硬的」，存留在 soft 与 soften 中，描述质地而不是价值。

items.en: Waru meant 'goods, merchandise, a commodity'; the same noun gives ware, warehouse and the -ware of silverware.
items.cn: waru 意为「货物、商品」，同一个名词衍生出 ware、warehouse 以及 silverware 里的 -ware。

items.en: English already used -ware for classes of goods, as in ironware, glassware and silverware, before any computing sense existed.
items.cn: 在计算机义出现之前，英语已用 -ware 表示一类货物，如 ironware、glassware 与 silverware。

items.en: The computing compound was formed in the 1950s by analogy with hardware: hard goods are the metal, soft goods are the instructions.
items.cn: 这个计算机复合词在二十世纪五十年代仿 hardware 造出：硬货物是金属，软货物是指令。

items.en: By the 1960s the word regularly meant programs and data as distinct from the machines that run them.
items.cn: 到二十世纪六十年代，这个词已稳定指程序与数据，与运行它们的机器相区别。

items.en: First printed use uncertain: the word is a transparent English compound of soft and ware, coined as the counterpart of hardware, so its formation is not in doubt; only the exact first printed use is not settled, and it is generally dated to the late 1950s rather than to a single documented sentence.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：这个词是 soft 与 ware 构成的透明英语复合词，作为 hardware 的对举而造，构词方式并不存疑；只是最早书证的具体出处尚无定论，一般把它定在二十世纪五十年代末，而非某一句有据可查的话。

note.en: Group one pulls apart the two halves of the compound and its -ware relatives; group two lists the things people actually call software in daily speech.
note.cn: 第一组拆开这个复合词的两半以及它的 -ware 亲属；第二组是日常说法里人们真正称为软件的东西。

entries.definition: An adjective for something yielding to pressure; alone it says nothing about programs.
entries.definitionCN: 形容受压会变形的事物；单独使用时与程序无关。

entries.definition: Goods or merchandise, now mostly in compounds such as silverware and hardware.
entries.definitionCN: 货物或商品，现在多出现在 silverware、hardware 这类复合词里。

entries.definition: Programs fixed into a chip, neither fully soft nor fully hard; formed on the same ware pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 固化在芯片里的程序，既不全软也不全硬；按同样的 ware 模式构成。

entries.definition: Programs written to damage or intrude; the mal- prefix marks intent, not texture.
entries.definitionCN: 为破坏或入侵而写的程序；mal- 前缀标记意图，而非质地。

entries.definition: A single ordered set of instructions; software can mean one program or a whole collection.
entries.definitionCN: 一套有序的指令；software 既可指一个程序，也可指整个集合。

entries.definition: A program written for a task the user performs; narrower than software, which includes the system layer.
entries.definitionCN: 为用户执行的任务而写的程序；比 software 窄，后者还包含系统层。

entries.definition: The source text a programmer writes; software includes code but also data, builds and documentation.
entries.definitionCN: 程序员写下的源文本；software 还包含数据、构建产物与文档。

entries.definition: A set of programs distributed together; it stresses the wrapping and delivery rather than the material.
entries.definitionCN: 一起分发的一组程序；强调包装与交付，而非材料本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: soft goods, the -ware family and the industry that sells them.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：软货物、-ware 一族，以及出售它们的产业。

normal.en: Soft is the opposite of hard, and ware means goods: goods you cannot hold.
normal.cn: soft 与 hard 相对，ware 意为货物：拿不到的货物。

normal.en: The old sense of ware survives in silverware, glassware and warehouse.
normal.cn: ware 的旧义存留在 silverware、glassware 与 warehouse 里。

normal.en: Firmware sits between the two, fixed in a chip.
normal.cn: firmware 夹在两者之间，固定在芯片里。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: software engineer, software development, application software.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：软件工程师、软件开发、应用软件。

normal.en: Trade talk sells software by subscription rather than by box.
normal.cn: 商业说法里，软件按月订阅出售，而不是装盒卖。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe card doing the work while the kitchen stays empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一张菜谱卡在干活，厨房里却空无一物。

abstract.en: Picture a switchboard of rules flipping before any metal moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一块规则开关板在金属动起来之前先翻动。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose habits were installed by long training.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人，他的习惯是长期训练装进去的。

examples.en: Open-source software can be inspected, changed and redistributed by anyone.
examples.cn: 开源软件任何人都能查看、修改与再分发。

examples.en: The company now earns more from software than from the machines it runs on.
examples.cn: 这家公司如今从软件赚到的钱，比从运行软件的机器赚到的更多。

examples.en: Bugs in the software appeared only when the network was slow.
examples.cn: 软件里的缺陷只在网络变慢时才出现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「soft（软）+ ware（物件）」——不是硬件的那些东西：程序与数据

root: soft 出自古英语 sōfte「柔软」，ware 出自古英语 waru「货物、商品」；二十世纪中期仿 hardware 造出，指与机器相对的指令与数据。属英语本族复合词，没有拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image of soft goods: the whole collection, one product, the system layer, the application layer, an industry, the written code, bundled installs and the metaphor of a trained mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个「软货物」意象：整体集合、单个产品、系统层、应用层、一个产业、写下的源码、捆绑预装，以及被训练过的头脑这一比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: goods that are soft — instructions and data you cannot hold, set against the metal you can.
core.cn: 核心意象：软的货物——拿不到的指令与数据，与拿得到的金属相对。

chain: THE LAYER NEXT TO THE MACHINE

branches.en: THE WHOLE STOCK: programs and data counted together, the way goods are counted in a warehouse.
branches.cn: 整批存货：程序与数据合在一起算，像仓库里清点货物。

branches.en: ONE ITEM ON THE SHELF: a single title that a user installs, opens and curses.
branches.cn: 货架上的一件：用户安装、打开、偶尔咒骂的单个产品。

branches.en: TWO LAYERS: system goods sit next to the machine, application goods sit next to the user.
branches.cn: 两层：系统货物贴近机器，应用货物贴近用户。

branches.en: GOODS THAT TRAVEL: an industry makes them, a device ships with them already inside.
branches.cn: 会走路的货物：一个产业制造它们，一台设备出厂时就带着它们。

branches.en: TEXT AND MIND: the written code exists before it runs, and the metaphor moves the same goods into a head.
branches.cn: 文本与头脑：写下的源码先于运行存在，比喻又把同样的货物搬进脑袋。

intro.en: Software is a native English compound, so its parts come from Old English rather than from Latin or Greek.
intro.cn: software 是英语本族复合词，各部分出自古英语，而非拉丁语或希腊语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: soft and ware are Old English words, and the compound was coined in modern English. The -ware seen in firmware and malware is the same native element, not a Latin suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁来源：soft 与 ware 都是古英语词，复合词是在现代英语中造的。firmware 与 malware 里看到的 -ware 仍是同一个本族成分，并非拉丁词尾。

items.example: Soft describes the goods, not the quality of the code.
items.exampleCN: soft 描述货物本身，不评价代码好坏。

items.example: Soften means to make something soft.
items.exampleCN: soften 意为使某物变软。

items.example: Ware survives in compounds rather than alone.
items.exampleCN: ware 多存留于复合词中，很少单独使用。

items.example: Silverware and glassware both use this pattern.
items.exampleCN: silverware 与 glassware 都用这个构词模式。

items.example: Hardware supplied the model for the later coinage.
items.exampleCN: hardware 为后来的新造词提供了样板。

items.example: The compound was formed as the opposite of hardware.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是作为 hardware 的对举而造的。

items.example: Firmware changes rarely and only with a special tool.
items.exampleCN: 固件很少变动，且需专用工具才能改。

items.example: Malware hides inside files that look ordinary.
items.exampleCN: 恶意软件藏在看似普通的文件里。

items.example: The old sense of ware as goods is clear in warehouse.
items.exampleCN: ware 的「货物」旧义在 warehouse 里很清楚。

items.example: Software engineering covers testing, design and maintenance.
items.exampleCN: 软件工程涵盖测试、设计与维护。

definition_zh: 硬件；计算机的物理设备；某个具体部件；五金件与金属配件；家用或工场工具；军事装备；与软件相对的物质层；体育俚语里的奖杯；美式口语里的五金店
definition_en: the physical equipment of a computer or other machine, and more broadly metal goods, tools, military equipment or, in slang, a trophy
core_image: 手里掂着的一把螺栓和铰链，沉、硬、有重量
scene: 工场角落的木架上摆着螺栓、铰链和几卷铜线，旁边是一台拆开的旧机器。The hardware in the workshop included bolts, hinges and sheets of galvanised steel.
sceneCN: 这里 hardware 指「五金件与金属配件」（第 3 个义项：金属制的零件与配件）；句意：工场里的五金件包括螺栓、铰链和几片镀锌钢板。图中可辨识物件：木架、螺栓、铰链、铜线卷、拆开的旧机器。

pos.zh: 通常不可数，指设备或五金的总称

forms.label: 固定形式（不可数，一般无复数）

senses.title: The physical parts of a computer
senses.definition: the physical parts of a computer or network, such as the processor, memory, drives and display
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或网络的物理部件，如处理器、内存、驱动器与显示器
senses.example: The hardware includes the processor, memory and display.
senses.exampleCN: 硬件包括处理器、内存与显示器。
senses.why: The old word for iron goods was extended to the metal of a computer, because both are the solid part one can touch.
senses.whyCN: 指铁器的旧词被扩展到计算机的金属部分，因为两者都是能摸到的实心部分。

senses.title: One component or device
senses.definition: one physical unit or component, viewed as an item to be fitted, replaced or repaired
senses.definitionCN: 单个物理单元或部件，被视为可安装、更换或修理的一件东西
senses.example: One faulty piece of hardware caused the whole rack to restart.
senses.exampleCN: 一个出故障的硬件部件让整机架重启。
senses.why: Counted by the piece, the mass noun takes the phrase piece of and names a single unit.
senses.whyCN: 按件计数时，这个不可数名词用「一件」这样的量词来指单个单元。

senses.title: Metal fittings and parts
senses.definition: metal fittings and accessories for doors, furniture or buildings, such as hinges, handles and screws
senses.definitionCN: 用于门、家具或建筑的金属配件，如铰链、把手与螺钉
senses.example: The drawer handles are hardware, not part of the cabinet itself.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉把手属于五金件，不算柜体本身。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: hard goods sold by weight and by piece for building and repair.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：按重量和件数出售、用于建造与修理的硬货物。

senses.title: Tools for home or workshop
senses.definition: the tools and implements kept for household repairs or workshop jobs
senses.definitionCN: 为家庭修理或工场作业而备的工具与器具
senses.example: He keeps his hardware in a tin box under the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 他把工具收在长凳下的铁皮箱里。
senses.why: A store that sold fittings also sold tools, and the word covered the whole stock.
senses.whyCN: 卖配件的店也卖工具，这个词就覆盖了整批货。

senses.title: Military equipment
senses.definition: weapons, vehicles and other heavy equipment used by armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 武装部队使用的武器、车辆与其他重型装备
senses.example: The treaty limited the heavy hardware each side could deploy.
senses.exampleCN: 条约限制双方可部署的重型装备。
senses.why: Armies need hard goods in quantity, so military writing borrowed the commercial word.
senses.whyCN: 军队需要大量硬货物，军事写作便借用了这个商业词。

senses.title: The material layer of a system
senses.definition: the physical layer of a system, considered apart from the programs and rules that direct it
senses.definitionCN: 系统的物理层，与指挥它的程序及规则分开看待
senses.example: No change in the hardware could fix a fault in the logic.
senses.exampleCN: 硬件怎么改都修不好逻辑里的错误。
senses.why: Once programs were called soft goods, the metal needed the opposite label, and hardware supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 程序既被称为软货物，金属就需要一个相反的标签，hardware 正好补上。

senses.title: Sports slang for a trophy
senses.definition: informal use for a trophy, medal or championship prize
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指奖杯、奖牌或冠军奖品
senses.example: The captain lifted the hardware above his head.
senses.exampleCN: 队长把奖杯举过头顶。
senses.why: A trophy is a hard, shiny object held up for a crowd, so slang calls it hard goods too.
senses.whyCN: 奖杯是坚硬发亮、举给人群看的东西，俚语便也把它叫作硬货物。

senses.title: American short form for the shop
senses.titleCN: 美式口语里对五金店的简称
senses.definition: in American speech, a shortened way of referring to a shop that sells tools and fittings
senses.definitionCN: 美式口语中，对出售工具与配件之店铺的简称
senses.example: I stopped at the hardware for a box of nails.
senses.exampleCN: 我在五金店停了一下，买了一盒钉子。
senses.why: Shop names lose the second word in speech, leaving the material word to stand for the place.
senses.whyCN: 店铺名称在口语里丢掉后一个词，材料词就代指了地点。

intro.en: Hardware is a native English compound. Hard descends from Old English heard 'hard, firm', and ware from waru 'goods, merchandise'. The compound is recorded in the fifteenth century for iron goods and tools, and it was extended to computing equipment in the mid-twentieth century. It has no Latin source.
intro.cn: hardware 是英语本族复合词。hard 出自古英语 heard「坚硬的、牢固的」，ware 出自 waru「货物、商品」。这个复合词在十五世纪已指铁器与工具，二十世纪中期又扩展到计算机设备。它没有拉丁来源。

items.en: Heard meant 'hard, firm, severe'; it gives hard, hardly and hardship, and it names a texture before it names a material.
items.cn: heard 意为「坚硬的、牢固的、严厉的」，衍生出 hard、hardly 与 hardship，先指质地再指材料。

items.en: Waru meant 'goods, merchandise'; the same noun gives ware, warehouse and the -ware of silverware.
items.cn: waru 意为「货物、商品」，同一个名词衍生出 ware、warehouse 以及 silverware 里的 -ware。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the compound named iron goods, fittings and the tools a household or smith would buy.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，这个复合词已指铁器、配件以及家庭或铁匠会买的工具。

items.en: American towns labelled the shop that sold these goods a hardware store, and the phrase became a fixture of main street.
items.cn: 美国市镇把出售这类货物的店铺标作「五金店」，这个说法成了主街的固定景观。

items.en: The computing sense is generally dated to the 1950s, when the metal of a machine was set against its programs; first citation uncertain: the exact earliest use is not recorded.
items.cn: 计算机义一般定在二十世纪五十年代，当时机器的金属部分与它的程序被对照起来；首见年代不确定：最早用例的具体出处没有记录。

items.en: Later English added military equipment, sports slang for trophies, and the American habit of calling the shop the hardware.
items.cn: 后来的英语又添上军事装备、指奖杯的体育俚语，以及美国人把店铺直接简称作「五金店」的习惯。

note.en: Group one separates the two halves of the compound and its -ware relatives; group two lists words for equipment that differ in scope or concreteness.
note.cn: 第一组拆开这个复合词的两半及其 -ware 亲属；第二组是范围或具体程度不同的设备类词。

entries.definition: An adjective for firmness or difficulty; alone it says nothing about equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 表示坚硬或困难的形容词；单独使用时与设备无关。

entries.definition: Goods or merchandise, now mostly in compounds such as ironware and warehouse.
entries.definitionCN: 货物或商品，现在多出现在 ironware、warehouse 这类复合词里。

entries.definition: Programs fixed into a chip; it borrows the ware pattern and sits between the two extremes.
entries.definitionCN: 固化在芯片里的程序；借用 ware 的构词模式，位于两个极端之间。

entries.definition: Programs and data, the opposite number of hardware in the computing pair.
entries.definitionCN: 程序与数据，在计算机那对词里是 hardware 的对立项。

entries.definition: The things needed for a purpose, from cameras to gym gear; broader and less technical than hardware.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的所需的东西，从相机到健身器材；比 hardware 更宽、更不专业。

entries.definition: Machines considered collectively, often large and powered; hardware can be small fittings as well.
entries.definitionCN: 机器的集合称法，常指大型动力机械；hardware 也可以是小配件。

entries.definition: Devices that connect to a computer, such as keyboards and printers; a subset of hardware.
entries.definitionCN: 连接到计算机的设备，如键盘与打印机；是 hardware 的一个子集。

entries.definition: A set of equipment for a particular task, usually in a laboratory or formal description.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定任务配备的一套设备，常用于实验室或正式描述。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: hard goods, the -ware family, the old shop and the computing pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：硬货物、-ware 一族、老式店铺，以及计算机里的那对词。

normal.en: Hard is the opposite of soft, and ware means goods: goods you can hold and weigh.
normal.cn: hard 与 soft 相对，ware 意为货物：拿得到、称得出的货物。

normal.en: The old sense survives on a sign that says hardware store.
normal.cn: 旧义还活在写着「五金店」的招牌上。

normal.en: In computing the pair hardware and software splits metal from instructions.
normal.cn: 计算机里 hardware 与 software 这一对，把金属与指令分开。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: computer hardware, hardware failure, military hardware.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：计算机硬件、硬件故障、军事装备。

normal.en: Sports talk calls a trophy the hardware.
normal.cn: 体育说法把奖杯也叫作「硬件」。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of bolts and hinges sorted by size.
abstract.cn: 想象一排螺栓与铰链按尺寸排好。

abstract.en: Picture a bare circuit board before any instruction reaches it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块裸电路板，任何指令都还没到达。

abstract.en: Picture a tank and a trophy standing in the same warehouse, both called hardware.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆坦克与一座奖杯放在同一个仓库里，都被叫作 hardware。

examples.en: Upgrading the hardware rarely helps if the design is poor.
examples.cn: 如果设计本身很差，升级硬件也帮不上多少。

examples.en: The shop on the corner sells hardware, paint and garden tools.
examples.cn: 街角的店卖五金、油漆与园艺工具。

examples.en: Military hardware was moved to the border under cover of night.
examples.cn: 军事装备在夜色掩护下被运往边境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「hard（硬）+ ware（物件）」——硬邦邦的东西：设备、五金、装备

root: hard 出自古英语 heard「坚硬的」，ware 出自古英语 waru「货物、商品」；十五世纪已指铁器与五金，二十世纪中期扩展为计算机硬件。属英语本族复合词，没有拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image of hard goods: a computer's parts, a single component, metal fittings, workshop tools, military equipment, the material layer, a trophy and a shop.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个「硬货物」意象：计算机的部件、单个组件、金属配件、工场工具、军事装备、物质层、奖杯，以及一家店铺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hard goods — the solid metal you can hold, weigh and break.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬货物——能拿、能称、能摔坏的实心金属。

chain: THE LAYER MACHINES ARE MADE OF
A TROPHY AND A SHOP SIGN

branches.en: METAL YOU CAN TOUCH: the machine's parts and any single unit you can fit or replace.
branches.cn: 摸得到的金属：机器的部件，以及任何可安装、可更换的单个单元。

branches.en: THE OLD COUNTER: hinges, handles and hammers sold by weight and by piece.
branches.cn: 老柜台：铰链、把手与锤子，按重量和件数出售。

branches.en: THE FIELD: weapons and vehicles are hard goods at the largest scale.
branches.cn: 战场：武器与车辆是最大尺度的硬货物。

branches.en: THE LAYER: what a system is made of, set against what directs it.
branches.cn: 那一层：系统由什么做成，与什么在指挥它相对。

branches.en: THE SHINE AND THE SIGN: a cup held overhead, a shop named after its stock.
branches.cn: 闪光与招牌：举过头顶的杯子，以存货命名的店铺。

intro.en: Hardware is a native English compound, built from an Old English adjective and an Old English noun; no Latin element enters it.
intro.cn: hardware 是英语本族复合词，由古英语形容词与古英语名词构成，没有拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: hard and ware are native words, and the compound is formed inside English. The -ware seen in firmware and software is the same native element, not a Latin suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁来源：hard 与 ware 都是本族词，复合词在英语内部构成。firmware 与 software 里看到的 -ware 仍是同一个本族成分，不是拉丁词尾。

items.example: Hard names the texture of the goods.
items.exampleCN: hard 道出货物的质地。

items.example: Harden means to make something hard.
items.exampleCN: harden 意为使某物变硬。

items.example: Ware now appears mostly inside compounds.
items.exampleCN: ware 现在多出现在复合词里。

items.example: Ironware and glassware follow this pattern.
items.exampleCN: ironware 与 glassware 都遵循这个模式。

items.example: The word began at the ironmonger's counter.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初出现在铁器商的柜台上。

items.meaning: a shop selling fittings and tools
items.meaningCN: 出售五金与工具的店铺
items.example: The sign over the door reads hardware store.
items.exampleCN: 门上的招牌写着「五金店」。

items.example: Software was coined as the contrasting compound.
items.exampleCN: software 是作为对举的复合词造出的。

items.example: Firmware sits between the two extremes.
items.exampleCN: 固件位于两个极端之间。

items.example: The old sense of ware as goods is clear here.
items.exampleCN: ware 的「货物」旧义在这里很清楚。

items.example: The design is hardware-based rather than simulated.
items.exampleCN: 该设计基于硬件，而非模拟。
